- [medium] "formatted_output": "# Command — stage-4-ux-interaction-architecture\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `stage-4-ux-interaction-architecture` command orchestrates Stage 4.\n\nIt transforms:\n\n* Stage 1 product workflows\n* Stage 2 validation findings\n* Stage 3 architecture outputs\n* user profiles\n* capabilities and feature structures\n* MVP boundaries\n\ninto:\n\n* user journey architecture\n* interaction architecture\n* screen system architecture\n* feature behavior specifications\n* state transition map\n* accessibility framework\n* implementation-ready UI blueprints\n* frontend build package\n\nThis is the Stage 4 command skill. It is not a single UX subskill.\n\n---\n\n# Cognitive Boundary\n\nStage 4 asks:\n\n```text\nHow should users move through and interact with the validated product?\n```\n\nStage 4 must not:\n\n* redefine the product concept\n* perform market validation\n* redesign backend system architecture\n* write implementation tickets\n* produce final UI art direction as decoration\n* generate frontend code\n* plan engineering sprints\n\nStage 4 may recommend product or architecture revisions only when interaction design exposes a blocking contradiction.\n\n---\n\n# Output Directory\n\nAll final Stage 4 outputs must be recorded in:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-4/\n```\n\nThe command must create this folder if it does not exist.\n\n---\n\n# Shared UX State\n\nThe command maintains a shared Stage 4 UX state object.\n\nThe shared UX state must be written to:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Build-status/UX-state.json\n```\n\nThe command must load this file at the beginning of Stage 4, update it after each UX skill runs, and preserve it as the durable interaction architecture state for the build.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"stage\": \"Stage 4\",\n  \"command\": \"stage-4-ux-interaction-architecture\",\n  \"status\": \"not_started\",\n  \"stage_1_inputs\": {},\n  \"stage_2_inputs\": {},\n  \"stage_3_inputs\": {},\n  \"preflight\": {},\n  \"user_journeys\": {},\n  \"interaction_architecture\": {},\n  \"screen_system\": {},\n  \"feature_behaviors\": {},\n  \"state_transition_map\": {},\n  \"accessibility_framework\": {},\n  \"ui_blueprints\": {},\n  \"page_inventory\": [],\n  \"interaction_contracts\": [],\n  \"interactive_element_inventory\": [],\n  \"route_inventory\": [],\n  \"action_inventory\": [],\n  \"navigation_inventory\": [],\n  \"visual_spec_inventory\": [],\n  \"design_system_foundation\": {},\n  \"visual_reference_selection\": {\n    \"primary_reference\": {},\n    \"secondary_references\": [],\n    \"rejected_references\": []\n  },\n  \"frontend_build_package\": {},\n  \"ux_decisions\": [],\n  \"ux_risks\": [],\n  \"interaction_tradeoffs\": [],\n  \"open_questions\": [],\n  \"interactive_guidance\": {\n    \"open_questions\": [],\n    \"answered_questions\": [],\n    \"assumptions_made\": [],\n    \"blocked_decisions\": [],\n    \"user_confirmations\": [],\n    \"ux_confidence_gaps\": []\n  },\n  \"stage_5_handoff\": {},\n  \"completion_status\": {}\n}\n```\n\nEach subskill reads the current UX state and writes its updates back into the shared state before the next skill runs.\n\nAfter each subskill completes, the command must persist the updated shared state to:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Build-status/UX-state.json\n```\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Rules\n\nThe Stage 4 command should behave like a guided interaction design interview.\n\nUse this decision rule:\n\n```text\nAsk only for UX decisions that materially affect user journeys, interaction behavior, screen structure, accessibility, or Stage 5 implementation planning.\nInfer standard interaction defaults when risk is low and the product workflow supports the inference.\nRecord assumptions when proceeding without user confirmation.\nBlock only when a missing decision prevents coherent interaction architecture.\n```\n\nWhen asking the user questions:\n\n* ask 1-3 questions at a time\n* prioritize workflow-blocking or accessibility-critical questions first\n* avoid asking questions already answered by Stage 1, Stage 2, or Stage 3 outputs\n* explain what journey, screen, state, or behavior each question affects\n* prefer concrete options over open-ended questions when the tradeoff is known\n* update `interactive_guidance.open_questions`\n* move answered questions into `interactive_guidance.answered_questions`\n* record inferred defaults in `interactive_guidance.assumptions_made`\n* record unresolved blockers in `interactive_guidance.blocked_decisions`\n\nThe command should continue automatically when a UX decision has a low-risk default.\n\nThe command should pause for user input when:\n\n* primary user journey is unclear\n* user role differences change screens or permissions\n* a workflow has no clear start, success, or failure state\n* feature behavior depends on an unresolved product decision\n* accessibility requirements materially affect interaction design\n* the screen system cannot support a core workflow\n* a Stage 3 architecture constraint changes user interaction\n\nThe command should not ask the user to choose implementation details that belong to Stage 5 unless the decision changes Stage 4 interaction architecture.\n\nFor every created page, infer a complete interactive element proposal before asking the user. A created page is any page or screen recorded in `page_inventory` or `ui_blueprints`.\n\nClassify each created page as:\n\n```text\nlaunch_critical\nstandard\nsupporting\ndeferred\n```\n\nPresent the proposed interactive elements for approval only when the choice materially changes workflow scope, permissions, destructive behavior, route or action outcomes, accessibility, or Stage 5 implementation. Ask the user to approve, remove, rename, reroute, or add elements. Record low-risk inferred elements in `interactive_guidance.assumptions_made`.\n\nEvery page interaction contract must use one approval status:\n\n```text\napproved\nassumed_low_risk\nneeds_user_review\nblocked\n```\n\n---\n\n# Stage 4 Input Contract\n\nLoad Stage 1 outputs from:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-1/\n```\n\nLoad Stage 2 outputs from:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-2/\n```\n\nLoad Stage 3 outputs from:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-3/\n```\n\nRequired Stage 1 files:\n\n```text\n02-user-system-map.json\n03-workflow-architecture.json\n04-product-capabilities.json\n05-feature-structure.json\n06-product-boundaries.json\n08-mvp-operational-model.json\n10-success-framework.json\n```\n\nRequired Stage 2 files:\n\n```text\n01-market-analysis.json\n05-risk-validation.json\n06-strategic-positioning.json\n```\n\nRequired Stage 3 files:\n\n```text\n01-system-topology.json\n02-service-architecture.json\n03-data-architecture.json\n04-api-architecture.json\n06-security-foundations.json\n08-scalability-framework.json\n```\n\nMinimum viable input set:\n\n```text\nStage 1:\n02-user-system-map.json\n03-workflow-architecture.json\n05-feature-structure.json\n08-mvp-operational-model.json\n\nStage 3:\n01-system-topology.json\n03-data-architecture.json\n04-api-architecture.json\n", (Source: `Rebuilding Stage 4 commands skills.md`)

UI blueprints that can be consumed by frontend design skills, frontend builder skills, task generators, and agent builders without generating frontend code.\n\nThis is the Stage 4 command skill. - [medium] "formatted_output": "# Command — stage-4-ux-interaction-architecture\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `stage-4-ux-interaction-architecture` command orchestrates Stage 4.\n\nIt transforms:\n\n* Stage 1 product workflows\n* Stage 2 validation findings\n* Stage 3 architecture outputs\n* user profiles\n* capabilities and feature structures\n* MVP boundaries\n\ninto:\n\n* user journey architecture\n* interaction architecture\n* screen system architecture\n* feature behavior specifications\n* state transition map\n* accessibility framework\n* implementation-ready UI blueprints\n* frontend build package\n\nThis is the Stage 4 command skill. It is not a single UX subskill.\n\n---\n\n# Cognitive Boundary\n\nStage 4 asks:\n\n```text\nHow should users move through and interact with the validated product?\n```\n\nStage 4 must not:\n\n* redefine the product concept\n* perform market validation\n* redesign backend system architecture\n* write implementation tickets\n* produce final UI art direction as decoration\n* generate frontend code\n* plan engineering sprints\n\nStage 4 may recommend product or architecture revisions only when interaction design exposes a blocking contradiction.\n\n---\n\n# Output Directory\n\nAll final Stage 4 outputs must be recorded in:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-4/\n```\n\nThe command must create this folder if it does not exist.\n\n---\n\n# Shared UX State\n\nThe command maintains a shared Stage 4 UX state object.\n\nThe shared UX state must be written to:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Build-status/UX-state.json\n```\n\nThe command must load this file at the beginning of Stage 4, update it after each UX skill runs, and preserve it as the durable interaction architecture state for the build.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"stage\": \"Stage 4\",\n  \"command\": \"stage-4-ux-interaction-architecture\",\n  \"status\": \"not_started\",\n  \"stage_1_inputs\": {},\n  \"stage_2_inputs\": {},\n  \"stage_3_inputs\": {},\n  \"preflight\": {},\n  \"user_journeys\": {},\n  \"interaction_architecture\": {},\n  \"screen_system\": {},\n  \"feature_behaviors\": {},\n  \"state_transition_map\": {},\n  \"accessibility_framework\": {},\n  \"ui_blueprints\": {},\n  \"page_inventory\": [],\n  \"interaction_contracts\": [],\n  \"interactive_element_inventory\": [],\n  \"route_inventory\": [],\n  \"action_inventory\": [],\n  \"navigation_inventory\": [],\n  \"visual_spec_inventory\": [],\n  \"design_system_foundation\": {},\n  \"visual_reference_selection\": {\n    \"primary_reference\": {},\n    \"secondary_references\": [],\n    \"rejected_references\": []\n  },\n  \"frontend_build_package\": {},\n  \"ux_decisions\": [],\n  \"ux_risks\": [],\n  \"interaction_tradeoffs\": [],\n  \"open_questions\": [],\n  \"interactive_guidance\": {\n    \"open_questions\": [],\n    \"answered_questions\": [],\n    \"assumptions_made\": [],\n    \"blocked_decisions\": [],\n    \"user_confirmations\": [],\n    \"ux_confidence_gaps\": []\n  },\n  \"stage_5_handoff\": {},\n  \"completion_status\": {}\n}\n```\n\nEach subskill reads the current UX state and writes its updates back into the shared state before the next skill runs.\n\nAfter each subskill completes, the command must persist the updated shared state to:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Build-status/UX-state.json\n```\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Rules\n\nThe Stage 4 command should behave like a guided interaction design interview.\n\nUse this decision rule:\n\n```text\nAsk only for UX decisions that materially affect user journeys, interaction behavior, screen structure, accessibility, or Stage 5 implementation planning.\nInfer standard interaction defaults when risk is low and the product workflow supports the inference.\nRecord assumptions when proceeding without user confirmation.\nBlock only when a missing decision prevents coherent interaction architecture.\n```\n\nWhen asking the user questions:\n\n* ask 1-3 questions at a time\n* prioritize workflow-blocking or accessibility-critical questions first\n* avoid asking questions already answered by Stage 1, Stage 2, or Stage 3 outputs\n* explain what journey, screen, state, or behavior each question affects\n* prefer concrete options over open-ended questions when the tradeoff is known\n* update `interactive_guidance.open_questions`\n* move answered questions into `interactive_guidance.answered_questions`\n* record inferred defaults in `interactive_guidance.assumptions_made`\n* record unresolved blockers in `interactive_guidance.blocked_decisions`\n\nThe command should continue automatically when a UX decision has a low-risk default.\n\nThe command should pause for user input when:\n\n* primary user journey is unclear\n* user role differences change screens or permissions\n* a workflow has no clear start, success, or failure state\n* feature behavior depends on an unresolved product decision\n* accessibility requirements materially affect interaction design\n* the screen system cannot support a core workflow\n* a Stage 3 architecture constraint changes user interaction\n\nThe command should not ask the user to choose implementation details that belong to Stage 5 unless the decision changes Stage 4 interaction architecture.\n\nFor every created page, infer a complete interactive element proposal before asking the user. A created page is any page or screen recorded in `page_inventory` or `ui_blueprints`.\n\nClassify each created page as:\n\n```text\nlaunch_critical\nstandard\nsupporting\ndeferred\n```\n\nPresent the proposed interactive elements for approval only when the choice materially changes workflow scope, permissions, destructive behavior, route or action outcomes, accessibility, or Stage 5 implementation. Ask the user to approve, remove, rename, reroute, or add elements. Record low-risk inferred elements in `interactive_guidance.assumptions_made`.\n\nEvery page interaction contract must use one approval status:\n\n```text\napproved\nassumed_low_risk\nneeds_user_review\nblocked\n```\n\n---\n\n# Stage 4 Input Contract\n\nLoad Stage 1 outputs from:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-1/\n```\n\nLoad Stage 2 outputs from:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-2/\n```\n\nLoad Stage 3 outputs from:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-3/\n```\n\nRequired Stage 1 files:\n\n```text\n02-user-system-map.json\n", (Source: `Rebuilding Stage 4 commands skills.md`)
- [medium] "formatted_output": "# Skill — ui-blueprint-specification\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `ui-blueprint-specification` skill transforms Stage 4 UX requirements into implementation-ready UI blueprints without generating frontend code.\n\nIt defines:\n\n* pages\n* screens\n* layouts\n* components\n* navigation\n* user actions\n* forms\n* tables\n* cards\n* modals\n* drawers\n* loading states\n* empty states\n* error states\n* frontend build package inputs\n\nThis skill is the bridge between Stage 4 UX architecture and Stage 5 frontend implementation planning.\n\nIt consumes the selected Stage 4 design system and visual references from `design-system-foundation`. It applies those decisions per page instead of inventing a separate visual direction for each blueprint.\n\n---\n\n# Operating Rule\n\nDo not ask broad questions such as:\n\n```text\nWhat should this dashboard look like?\n```\n\nForce every launch-critical page through the page-definition matrix:\n\n```text\nPAGE\nPurpose\nPrimary User\nScreen Type\nLayout Type\nSections\nComponents\nActions\nData Needed\nStates\nValidation\nNavigation\n```\n\nThen force every launch-critical page through the visual spec matrix:\n\n```text\nVISUAL SPEC\nVisual Style\nDesign System Refs\nVisual Reference Refs\nDensity\nColor Direction\nTypography Feel\nComponent Style\nPrimary Visual Focus\nResponsive Behavior\nVisual Do Rules\nVisual Don't Rules\nReference Apps\nDesign System Alignment\nVisual Acceptance Criteria\nUser Approval Status\n```\n\n---\n\n# Controlled Choices\n\nScreen type options:\n\n```text\nDashboard\nList\nDetail View\nForm\nWizard\nSettings\nProfile\nAnalytics\nMessaging\nLanding Page\nHero Page\nMarketing Page\nOnboarding\nPricing\nAuthentication\nAdmin\nCheckout\nCustom\n```\n\nScreen/page type selection must be contextual.\n\nThese options are a controlled vocabulary, not a required checklist. Include only page or screen types justified by:\n\n* Stage 1 product category and MVP scope\n* Stage 1 workflows and feature structure\n* Stage 3 selected stack and architecture constraints\n* Stage 4 user journeys and launch-critical interactions\n* user roles, permissions, and navigation needs\n\nDo not add `Landing Page`, `Hero Page`, `Dashboard`, `Admin`, `Checkout`, `Authentication`, `Pricing`, or any other page type unless the product model requires it.\n\nFor each selected page type, record:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"page_name\": \"\",\n  \"screen_type\": \"\",\n  \"included_because\": [],\n  \"source_refs\": [],\n  \"excluded_page_types\": [\n    {\n      \"screen_type\": \"\",\n      \"reason\": \"\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nAsk the user only when a launch-critical page type is ambiguous. Otherwise infer the page type from upstream workflow, role, feature, and route evidence, and record the assumption.\n\nLayout type options:\n\n```text\nSidebar\nTop Navigation\nSplit View\nCard Grid\nTable\nMobile First\nFull Screen\nCustom\n```\n\nComponent options:\n\n```text\nCards\nCharts\nTables\nSearch\nFilters\nForms\nTabs\nModals\nDrawers\nNotifications\nFile Upload\nComments\nTimeline\nMaps\nCalendar\n```\n\nAction options:\n\n```text\nCreate\nRead\nUpdate\nDelete\nExport\nShare\nInvite\nApprove\nReject\nUpload\nDownload\n```\n\nVisual style options:\n\n```text\nMinimal\nEnterprise\nEditorial\nConsumer App\nSaaS Dashboard\nData Dense\nPlayful\nLuxury\nUtility\nCustom\n```\n\nDensity options:\n\n```text\nCompact\nBalanced\nSpacious\nData Dense\nMobile First\nCustom\n```\n\nComponent style options:\n\n```text\nFlat\nOutlined\nSoft Card\nHigh Contrast\nDense Utility\nMedia Rich\nCustom\n```\n\n---\n\n# Complete App Blueprint Markdown\n\nGenerate a readable complete app blueprint tree at:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-4/09-complete-app-blueprint.md\n```\n\nThe markdown tree must use this structure, adapted to the app being built. The example page names below are illustrative only; the generated tree must include the pages required by the actual product:\n\n```text\nComplete App Blueprint\n│\n├── Pages\n│   ├── Example Landing Page\n│   │   ├── Hero\n│   │   ├── Feature Preview\n│   │   ├── CTA\n│   │   └── Footer\n│   ├── Example Dashboard\n│   │   ├── Summary Cards\n│   │   ├── Activity Feed\n│   │   └── Task Table\n│\n├── Components\n│\n├── Shared Components\n│\n├── Navigation\n│\n├── Routes\n│\n├── Actions\n│\n├── States\n│\n├── Data Requirements\n│\n└── Frontend Build Package\n```\n\nEvery launch-critical page in the markdown tree must map to a `ui_blueprint_id` and include its sections, components, primary actions, route, states, and data requirements.\n\nThe complete app blueprint must also include:\n\n* one compact Mermaid app route map covering every created page\n* page-level Mermaid interaction maps for launch-critical or complex pages\n* critical workflow Mermaid maps that include success, failure, and recovery branches\n* destructive or mutation Mermaid maps that include confirmation and result states\n\nRequire a page-level Mermaid map when a page has multiple interaction branches, destructive or mutation actions, modal or drawer flows, or complex routing. A trivial page may rely on its interaction contract and inventories when the app route map already covers it.\n\n---\n\n# Visual Hierarchy Model\n\nEach page blueprint must preserve:\n\n```text\nPage\n├─ Section\n│  ├─ Component\n│  │  ├─ Interactive Element\n│  │  │  └─ Route, Action, Or No Navigation\n│  │  ├─ Data Source\n│  │  ├─ Validation\n│  │  └─ States\n```\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Element Schema\n\nEvery interactive element on a page (button, link, icon button, menu item, tab, input, etc.) must be enumerated with:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"element_id\": \"UI-ELEMENT-001\",\n  \"element_type\": \"button | link | icon_button | menu_item | tab | toggle | checkbox | radio | select | text_input | search_input | file_upload | date_picker | breadcrumb | pagination | clickable_card | clickable_row | disclosure\",\n  \"label\": \"\",\n  \"accessible_name\": \"\",\n  \"icon\": \"\",\n  \"owning_page_ref\": \"\",\n  \"owning_section_ref\": \"\",\n  \"owning_component_ref\": \"\",\n  \"route_id\": \"\",\n  \"route_target\": \"\",\n  \"route_type\": \"internal_page | external_url | modal | drawer | anchored_section | file_download | api_action | state_transition | no_navigation\",\n  \"action_id\": \"ACTION-001\",\n  \"behavior\": \"navigate | submit | open_modal | open_drawer | toggle | trigger_action | open_link | download | call_api | scroll_to | no_navigation\",\n  \"behavior_target\": \"\",\n  \"design_system_component\": \"\",\n  \"states\": {\n    \"default\": {},\n    \"loading\": {},\n    \"disabled\": {},\n    \"active\": {},\n    \"hover\": {}\n  },\n  \"permission_required\": \"\",\n  \"permission_denied_behavior\": \"\",\n  \"confirmation_required\": false,\n  \"responsive_behavior\": {},\n  \"accessibility_behavior\": {},\n  \"analytics_event\": \"\",\n  \"source_trace\": []\n}\n```\n\n# Action Inventory Schema\n\nEvery action across all pages must be recorded in a global action inventory:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"action_id\": \"ACTION-001\",\n  \"name\": \"\",\n  \"element_type\": \"button | link | icon_button | menu_item | tab | toggle | checkbox | radio | select\",\n  \"label\": \"\",\n  \"route_target\": \"\",\n  \"behavior\": \"navigate | submit | open_modal | open_drawer | toggle | trigger_action | open_link | download | call_api | scroll_to\",\n  \"behavior_target\": \"\",\n  \"owning_page_refs\": [],\n  \"owning_component_refs\": [],\n  \"triggering_element_refs\": [],\n  \"permission_required\": \"\",\n  \"confirmation_required\": false,\n  \"success_destination\": \"\",\n  \"failure_destination\": \"\",\n  \"loading_state\": \"\",\n  \"empty_state\": \"\",\n  \"permission_denied_behavior\": \"\",\n  \"undo_or_recovery_path\": \"\",\n It is not a single UX subskill.\n\n---\n\n# Cognitive Boundary\n\nStage 4 asks:\n\n```text\nHow should users move through and interact with the validated product?\n```\n\nStage 4 must not:\n\n* Stage 4 outputs must be recorded in:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-4/\n```\n\nThe command must create this folder if it does not exist.\n\n---\n\n# Shared UX State\n\nThe command maintains a shared Stage 4 UX state object.\n\nThe shared UX state must be written to:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Build-status/UX-state.json\n```\n\nThe command must load this file at the beginning of Stage 4, update it \"stage-4-ux-interaction-architecture\",\n  \"status\": \"not_started\",\n  \"stage_1_inputs\": {},\n  \"stage_2_inputs\": {},\n  \"stage_3_inputs\": {},\n  \"preflight\": {},\n  \"user_journeys\": - [medium] "formatted_output": "# Orchestrated Skills\n\nRun Stage 4 skills in this order:\n\n```text\n1. user-journey-design\n2. interaction-architecture-design\n3. screen-system-design\n4. feature-behavior-specification\n5. state-transition-and-accessibility-design\n6. design-system-foundation\n7. ui-blueprint-specification\n8. ux-interaction-synthesis\n```\n\n---\n\n# Skill — user-journey-design\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `user-journey-design` skill defines the main user journeys and outcome paths.\n\nIt determines:\n\n* primary user journeys\n* secondary user journeys\n* entry points\n* success states\n* failure states\n* role-specific journey differences\n* MVP journey boundaries\n\n---\n\n# Core Responsibilities\n\n## Journey Mapping\n\nDefine:\n\n* user goals\n* journey start states\n* user actions\n* system responses\n* decision points\n* success outcomes\n* failure outcomes\n* recovery paths\n\n## Role and Persona Mapping\n\nMap journeys across:\n\n* primary users\n* secondary users\n* admins or operators\n* guest or unauthenticated users\n* permission-based user roles\n\n## Journey Risk Detection\n\nIdentify:\n\n* missing user goals\n* unclear success states\n* excessive friction\n* unsupported failure recovery\n* role conflicts\n* MVP journey gaps\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Responsibilities\n\nThis skill should guide the user only when journeys cannot be inferred safely.\n\nAsk targeted questions when any of these are unclear:\n\n* primary user goal\n* first action in the journey\n* successful end state\n* failure or recovery behavior\n* role-specific journey differences\n* whether a journey is MVP-critical or deferred\n\nInfer common journey defaults when the workflow and user profile make them obvious, but record the assumption in:\n\n```text\ninteractive_guidance.assumptions_made\n```\n\nPause for user input when a journey decision changes screens, permissions, feature behavior, or MVP scope.\n\n---\n\n# Inputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user_profiles\": {},\n  \"workflows\": {},\n  \"feature_structure\": {},\n  \"mvp_scope\": {},\n  \"existing_state\": {}\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Outputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user_journeys\": {},\n  \"journey_roles\": [],\n  \"entry_points\": [],\n  \"success_states\": [],\n  \"failure_states\": [],\n  \"journey_risks\": [],\n  \"open_questions\": []\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Shared State Updates\n\n```text\nuser_journeys\nux_decisions\nux_risks\nopen_questions\ninteractive_guidance\n```\n\n---\n\n# Skill — interaction-architecture-design\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `interaction-architecture-design` skill defines how users interact with product workflows and system responses.\n\nIt determines:\n\n* interaction patterns\n* navigation model\n* decision points\n* command flows\n* feedback patterns\n* error and recovery interactions\n* role-based interaction differences\n\n---\n\n# Core Responsibilities\n\n## Interaction Model\n\nDefine:\n\n* navigation paths\n* action patterns\n* confirmation patterns\n* feedback and notification behavior\n* user input patterns\n* system response patterns\n* recovery behavior\n\n## Interaction Constraints\n\nMap constraints from:\n\n* system topology\n* APIs\n* permissions\n* data ownership\n* asynchronous processing\n* security requirements\n\n## Interaction Risk Detection\n\nIdentify:\n\n* confusing flows\n* missing feedback\n* hidden system delays\n* unsafe destructive actions\n* permission ambiguity\n* unsupported recovery paths\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Responsibilities\n\nThis skill should guide the user through interaction decisions that materially affect workflow usability.\n\nAsk targeted questions when any of these are unclear:\n\n* navigation model\n* whether a user action needs confirmation\n* how async processing should be communicated\n* how errors or failed actions should be handled\n* whether actions are reversible\n* how users move between related workflows\n* how permission limits should appear to users\n\nInfer standard interaction defaults when risk is low, but record the assumption in:\n\n```text\ninteractive_guidance.assumptions_made\n```\n\nPause for user input when an interaction decision changes workflow completion, safety, permissions, or recovery.\n\n---\n\n# Inputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user_journeys\": {},\n  \"workflows\": {},\n  \"api_architecture\": {},\n  \"security_foundations\": {},\n  \"existing_state\": {}\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Outputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"interaction_architecture\": {},\n  \"navigation_model\": {},\n  \"interaction_patterns\": [],\n  \"feedback_patterns\": [],\n  \"recovery_patterns\": [],\n  \"interaction_risks\": []\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Shared State Updates\n\n```text\ninteraction_architecture\nux_decisions\nux_risks\ninteraction_tradeoffs\ninteractive_guidance\n```\n\n---\n\n# Skill — screen-system-design\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `screen-system-design` skill defines the screen architecture needed to support user journeys and interactions.\n\nIt determines:\n\n* screens\n* screen groups\n* layout responsibilities\n* information hierarchy\n* navigation structure\n* role-based screen access\n* MVP screen boundaries\n\n---\n\n# Core Responsibilities\n\n## Screen Architecture\n\nDefine:\n\n* required screens\n* screen purpose\n* screen inputs\n* screen outputs\n* screen-level user actions\n* screen data requirements\n* screen permissions\n* screen relationships\n\n## Screen System Consistency\n\nValidate:\n\n* screens map to journeys\n* screens support feature behavior\n* screen groups are coherent\n* navigation is complete\n* MVP screens are not over-scoped\n\n## Screen Risk Detection\n\nIdentify:\n\n* missing screens\n* redundant screens\n* unclear screen ownership\n* overloaded screens\n* role-based access confusion\n* unsupported workflow steps\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Responsibilities\n\nThis skill should guide the user through screen decisions that affect workflow completeness or interface consistency.\n\nAsk targeted questions when any of these are unclear:\n\n* whether a workflow step needs its own screen\n* whether admin/operator screens are required\n* which screens are MVP-critical\n* how role-based access changes screens\n* whether a screen should support creation, editing, review, or reporting\n* whether a dashboard, detail view, or list view is needed\n\nInfer standard screen patterns when the journey is simple and low-risk.\n\nRecord assumptions in:\n\n```text\ninteractive_guidance.assumptions_made\n```\n\nPause for user input when screen architecture affects journey completion, permissions, or Stage 5 implementation scope.\n\n---\n\n# Inputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user_journeys\": {},\n  \"interaction_architecture\": {},\n  \"feature_structure\": {},\n  \"data_architecture\": {},\n  \"security_foundations\": {},\n  \"existing_state\": {}\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Outputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"screen_system\": {},\n  \"screen_groups\": [],\n  \"screen_inventory\": [],\n  \"navigation_structure\": {},\n  \"screen_risks\": [],\n  \"open_questions\": []\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Shared State Updates\n\n```text\nscreen_system\nux_decisions\nux_risks\nopen_questions\ninteractive_guidance\n```\n\n---\n\n# Skill — feature-behavior-specification\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `feature-behavior-specification` skill defines how product features behave in response to user actions and system conditions.\n\nIt determines:\n\n* feature behavior\n* user-triggered behavior\n* system-triggered behavior\n* validation rules\n* permission behavior\n* error behavior\n* empty, loading, success, and failure states\n\n---\n\n# Core Responsibilities\n\n## Behavior Specification\n\nDefine:\n\n* feature purpose\n* trigger actions\n* system responses\n* required inputs\n* expected outputs\n* validation rules\n* permission checks\n* error and recovery behavior\n\n## Behavior Consistency\n\nValidate:\n\n* feature behavior supports journeys\n* behavior aligns with APIs and data model\n* behavior respects permissions\n* behavior supports MVP scope\n* behavior exposes clear feedback\n\n## Behavior Risk Detection\n\nIdentify:\n\n* ambiguous feature behavior\n* missing validation rules\n* unsafe destructive behavior\n* unclear permissions\n* hidden async states\n* missing empty or error states\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Responsibilities\n\nThis skill should guide the user through feature behavior decisions that affect user trust, safety, and implementation clarity.\n\nAsk targeted questions when any of these are unclear:\n\n* what triggers a feature\n* what happens after a user action\n* what validation rules apply\n* what users can edit, delete, submit, approve, or cancel\n* how errors should be handled\n* whether actions are reversible\n* what states the feature must support\n\nInfer standard behavior only when feature purpose and workflow context are clear.\n\nRecord assumptions in:\n\n```text\ninteractive_guidance.assumptions_made\n```\n\nPause for user input when feature behavior affects safety, permissions, validation, or implementation scope.\n\n---\n\n# Inputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"feature_structure\": {},\n  \"user_journeys\": {},\n  \"interaction_architecture\": {},\n  \"screen_system\": {},\n  \"api_architecture\": {},\n  \"security_foundations\": {},\n  \"existing_state\": {}\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Outputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"feature_behaviors\": {},\n  \"behavior_rules\": [],\n  \"validation_rules\": [],\n  \"permission_behaviors\": [],\n  \"error_behaviors\": [],\n  \"behavior_risks\": []\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Shared State Updates\n\n```text\nfeature_behaviors\nux_decisions\nux_risks\ninteraction_tradeoffs\ninteractive_guidance\n```\n\n---\n\n# Skill — state-transition-and-accessibility-design\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `state-transition-and-accessibility-design` skill defines user-visible state transitions and accessibility foundations.\n\nIt determines:\n\n* workflow states\n* screen states\n* feature states\n* transition triggers\n* loading and async states\n* accessibility requirements\n* inclusive interaction constraints\n\n---\n\n# Core Responsibilities\n\n## State Transition Mapping\n\nDefine:\n\n* start states\n* intermediate states\n* success states\n* failure states\n* loading states\n* empty states\n* permission-denied states\n* transition triggers\n\n## Accessibility Framework\n\nDefine:\n\n* keyboard interaction requirements\n* screen reader expectations\n* focus management needs\n* contrast and readability needs\n* form accessibility requirements\n* error messaging accessibility\n* motion and animation constraints\n\n## State and Accessibility Risk Detection\n\nIdentify:\n\n* missing state transitions\n* unclear loading behavior\n* inaccessible interaction patterns\n* missing focus or keyboard behavior\n* unclear error messaging\n* visual-only feedback risks\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Responsibilities\n\nThis skill should guide the user through state and accessibility decisions that affect task completion and inclusive use.\n\nAsk targeted questions when any of these are unclear:\n\n* what states a workflow can enter\n* how users know something is processing\n* how users recover from failure\n* whether keyboard-only use is required\n* whether screen reader support is required\n* whether motion, timing, or contrast constraints matter\n* how permission-denied or unavailable states should behave\n\nInfer baseline accessibility requirements as required, not optional.\n\nRecord assumptions in:\n\n```text\ninteractive_guidance.assumptions_made\n```\n\nPause for user input when a state or accessibility decision affects core task completion or legal/compliance expectations.\n\n---\n\n# Inputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user_journeys\": {},\n  \"interaction_architecture\": {},\n  \"screen_system\": {},\n  \"feature_behaviors\": {},\n  \"security_foundations\": {},\n  \"existing_state\": {}\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Outputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"state_transition_map\": {},\n  \"workflow_states\": [],\n  \"screen_states\": [],\n  \"feature_states\": [],\n  \"accessibility_framework\": {},\n  \"accessibility_risks\": []\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Shared State Updates\n\n```text\nstate_transition_map\naccessibility_framework\nux_decisions\nux_risks\ninteractive_guidance\n```\n\n---\n\n# Skill — ui-blueprint-specification\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `ui-blueprint-specification` skill transforms UX requirements into implementation-ready UI blueprints without generating frontend code.\n\nIt defines:\n\n* pages\n* screens\n* layouts\n* components\n* navigation\n* user actions\n* states\n* forms\n* tables\n* cards\n* modals\n* drawers\n* empty states\n* loading states\n* error states\n* frontend build package inputs\n\nThis skill is the bridge between Stage 4 UX architecture and Stage 5 frontend implementation planning.\n\n---\n\n# Core Responsibilities\n\n## Page Definition Matrix\n\nForce each page or screen through a structured matrix:\n\n```text\nPAGE\nPurpose\nPrimary User\nScreen Type\nLayout Type\nSections\nComponents\nActions\nData Needed\nStates\nValidation\nNavigation\n```\n\nThe skill must ask controlled UI questions using screen type, layout type, component selection, and action mapping options instead of broad visual preference questions.\n\n## Visual Spec Matrix\n\nForce each launch-critical page or screen through a visual specification matrix:\n\n```text\nVISUAL SPEC\nVisual Style\nDensity\nColor Direction\nTypography Feel\nComponent Style\nPrimary Visual Focus\nResponsive Behavior\nVisual Do Rules\nVisual Don't Rules\nReference Apps\nVisual Acceptance Criteria\nUser Approval Status\n```\n\nThe visual spec matrix captures how the UI should visually feel and what the frontend builder must preserve. It must not generate frontend code or mockups.\n\n## Visual Hierarchy Modeling\n\nRepresent each page as:\n\n```text\nPage\n├─ Section\n│  ├─ Component\n│  │  ├─ Action\n│  │  ├─ Data Source\n│  │  ├─ Validation\n│  │  └─ States\n```\n\n## Frontend Build Package\n\nGenerate a frontend build package containing:\n\n* page inventory\n* component inventory\n* shared components\n* navigation inventory\n* route inventory\n* state inventory\n* action inventory\n* frontend tasks\n* recommended frontend skills\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Responsibilities\n\nAsk the user to confirm or choose:\n\n* screen type\n* layout type\n* sections\n* component selections\n* user actions\n* required states\n* shared components\n* route/navigation expectations\n* visual style\n* density\n* color direction\n* typography feel\n* component style\n* primary visual focus\n* visual do and don't rules\n* visual acceptance criteria\n* user approval status\n\nAsk no more than 1-3 page-definition questions at once.\n\nInfer common UI patterns when they are strongly implied by the screen type and workflow, but record them in:\n\n```text\ninteractive_guidance.assumptions_made\n```\n\nPause for user input when:\n\n* a launch-critical page lacks purpose\n* a screen type cannot be inferred\n* a layout choice materially affects navigation or implementation\n* required components or actions are ambiguous\n* required states are missing for a launch-critical interaction\n* visual style, density, or primary visual focus is missing for a launch-critical page\n* the user has not approved the visual spec for a launch-critical page\n\nUpdate:\n\n```text\ninteractive_guidance.open_questions\ninteractive_guidance.answered_questions\ninteractive_guidance.assumptions_made\ninteractive_guidance.blocked_decisions\ninteractive_guidance.ux_confidence_gaps\n```\n\n---\n\n# Inputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user_journeys\": {},\n  \"interaction_architecture\": {},\n  \"screen_system\": {},\n  \"feature_behaviors\": {},\n  \"state_transition_map\": {},\n  \"accessibility_framework\": {},\n  \"ui_blueprints\": {},\n  \"frontend_build_package\": {},\n  \"existing_state\": {}\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Outputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"ui_blueprints\": [],\n  \"page_inventory\": [],\n  \"component_inventory\": [],\n  \"visual_spec_inventory\": [],\n  \"visual_reference_selection\": {},\n  \"shared_components\": [],\n  \"navigation_inventory\": [],\n  \"route_inventory\": [],\n  \"state_inventory\": [],\n  \"action_inventory\": [],\n  \"frontend_build_package\": {},\n  \"visual_approval_status\": {},\n  \"frontend_task_hints\": [],\n  \"open_questions\": []\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Shared State Updates\n\n```text\nui_blueprints\nvisual_spec_inventory\nfrontend_build_package\nstage_5_handoff\nux_confidence_gaps\n```\n\n---\n\n# Skill — design-system-foundation\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `design-system-foundation` skill defines the shared design system that all Stage 4 UI blueprints must follow.\n\nIt produces an implementation-ready visual contract without generating frontend code.\n\nIt defines:\n\n* product visual personality\n", (Source: `Rebuilding Stage 4 commands skills.md`)

Validate template files\n\nEvery template must contain:\n\n```yaml\ntemplate_checks:\n  - valid-template-id\n  - version-defined\n  - category-defined\n  - suitable-for-defined\n  - unsuitable-for-defined\n  - structural-defaults-defined\n  - navigation-defined\n  - page-archetypes-defined\n  - layout-rules-defined\n  - responsive-strategy-defined\n  - states-defined\n  - accessibility-defined\n```\n\n## Step 34. Validate generated project files\n\n```yaml\noutput_checks:\n  - every-page-has-purpose\n  - every-page-has-primary-goal\n  - every-page-has-archetype\n  - every-page-has-layout\n  - every-page-has-responsive-rules\n  - every-data-page-has-system-states\n  - every-navigation-item-maps-to-page\n  - primary-actions-are-defined\n  - no-orphan-pages\n  - no-duplicate-component-responsibilities\n```\n\n## Step 35. Add contradiction rules\n\nDetect issues such as:\n\n```yaml\ncontradictions:\n  - mobile-first-product-using-desktop-only-navigation\n  - comparison-heavy-page-using-non-comparable-card-layout\n  - long-workflow-placed-inside-small-modal\n  - required-action-hidden-in-overflow-menu\n  - table-without-mobile-behavior\n  - multiple-primary-actions-on-one-page\n  - navigation-item-without-destination\n  - page-without-entry-point\n```\n\n## Step 36. Add completion scoring\n\n```yaml\ncompletion_score:\n  product-context:\n  navigation:\n  page-inventory:\n  page-layouts:\n  components:\n  interactions:\n  responsive:\n  states:\n  accessibility:\n  overall:\n```\n\nExample:\n\n```yaml\ncompletion_score:\n  product-context: 100\n  navigation: 100\n  page-inventory: 95\n  page-layouts: 90\n  components: 85\n  interactions: 90\n  responsive: 100\n  states: 75\n  accessibility: 80\n  overall: 89\n```\n\n## Phase 9 deliverables\n\n```text\nvalidation/TEMPLATE-CHECKLIST.md\nvalidation/OUTPUT-CHECKLIST.md\nvalidation/CONTRADICTION-RULES.md\nvalidation/COMPLETION-SCORING.md\n```\n\n---\n\n# Phase 10 — Test the System\n\n## Step 37. Create test product briefs\n\nUse products with different structural needs.\n\n```text\ntests/test-projects/\n├── marketing-product.md\n├── saas-record-manager.md\n├── ecommerce-store.md\n├── mobile-task-app.md\n└── hybrid-marketplace.md\n```\n\n## Step 38. Test generated outputs\n\nVerify that each output is structurally different.\n\nExpected distinctions:\n\n```text\nMarketing website\n→ top navigation, content sections, conversion paths\n\nSaaS dashboard\n→ sidebar, tables, dashboards, record management\n\nEcommerce storefront\n→ product grids, filters, cart, checkout\n\nMobile utility\n→ bottom navigation, short flows, bottom sheets\n```\n\n## Step 40. Record template gaps\n\n```yaml\ntemplate_gap:\n  test_project:\n  template:\n  missing_pattern:\n  repeated_across_projects:\n  recommended_resolution:\n```\n\nOnly add new templates or extensions when a gap appears repeatedly.\n\n## Phase 10 deliverables\n\n```text\ntests/TEST-CASES.md\ntests/SELECTION-RESULTS.md\ntests/OUTPUT-REVIEWS.md\ntests/TEMPLATE-GAPS.md\n```\n\n---\n\n# Phase 11 — Package the System as an Agent Skill\n\n## Step 41. Create the skill folder\n\n```text\ngenerating-ui-component-architecture/\n├── SKILL.md\n├── references/\n│   ├── TEMPLATE-SCHEMA.md\n│   ├── TEMPLATE-SELECTOR.md\n│   ├── NORMALIZED-VALUES.md\n│   ├── GENERATION-WORKFLOW.md\n│   ├── templates/\n│   ├── patterns/\n│   └── extensions/\n├── assets/\n│   └── UI-COMPONENTS.template.md\n└── scripts/\n    ├── validate_template.py\n    └── validate_output.py\n```\n\n## Step 42. Define the skill metadata\n\n```yaml\n---\nname: generating-ui-component-architecture\ndescription: >\n  Selects and adapts structural UI architecture templates for websites,\n  web applications, commerce systems, and mobile applications. Generates\n  a project-specific UI-COMPONENTS.md defining navigation, application\n  shells, page layouts, component families, responsive behavior, states,\n  and accessibility requirements.\n---\n```\n\n## Step 43. Define the skill instructions\n\n```text\n1. Inspect product documentation.\n2. Extract product type and workflows.\n3. Select the closest UI architecture template.\n4. Load only the relevant template and pattern references.\n5. Select necessary extensions.\n6. Adapt the template to the project.\n7. Generate UI-COMPONENTS.md.\n8. Validate the output.\n9. Report unresolved decisions and template deviations.\n```\n\n## Step 44. Add optional commands later\n\n```text\n/ui-template-select\n/ui-components-generate\n/ui-components-validate\n/ui-template-compare\n/ui-template-create\n```\n\nThe first version only needs:\n\n```text\n/ui-template-select\n/ui-components-generate\n```\n\n---\n\n# Phase 12 — Version and Maintain the System\n\n## Step 45. Create a template registry\n\n```yaml\ntemplates:\n  - id: marketing-website\n    category: website\n    version: 1.0.0\n    status: stable\n\n  - id: saas-dashboard\n    category: web-app\n    version: 1.0.0\n    status: stable\n\n  - id: ecommerce-storefront\n    category: commerce\n    version: 1.0.0\n    status: stable\n\n  - id: mobile-utility\n    category: mobile\n    version: 1.0.0\n    status: stable\n```\n\n## Step 46. Define version rules\n\n```yaml\nversioning:\n  major: Breaking schema or architectural changes\n  minor: New patterns, pages, or capabilities\n  patch: Corrections and clarification\n```\n\n## Step 47. Add change tracking\n\nCreate:\n\n```text\nTEMPLATE-REGISTRY.md\nCHANGELOG.md\n```\n\n## Step 48. Establish update rules\n\nUpdate a template when:\n\n* The same missing pattern appears in several projects.\n* A recommendation repeatedly produces poor results.\n* Two or more templates duplicate the same guidance.\n* A new platform convention becomes common.\n* A responsive rule repeatedly fails.\n* A recurring contradiction is discovered.\n\n---\n\n# Recommended Implementation Order\n\n## Milestone 1 — Core schema\n\nBuild:\n\n```text\nREADME.md\nTEMPLATE-SCHEMA.md\nNORMALIZED-VALUES.md\nbase-ui-architecture.md\nUI-COMPONENTS.template.md\n```\n\nSuccess condition:\n\nAll future templates can use the same structure.\n\n## Milestone 2 — Four starter templates\n\nBuild:\n\n```text\nmarketing-website.md\nsaas-dashboard.md\necommerce-storefront.md\nmobile-utility.md\n```\n\nSuccess condition:\n\nEach template produces a clearly different interface architecture.\n\n## Milestone 3 — Selector\n\nBuild:\n\n```text\nTEMPLATE-SELECTOR.md\nSELECTION-QUESTIONS.md\nSELECTION-MATRIX.md\n```\n\nSuccess condition:\n\nA product brief can be mapped to the correct template with reasons.\n\n## Milestone 4 — Generator\n\nBuild:\n\n```text\nGENERATION-WORKFLOW.md\nINPUT-SCHEMA.md\nOUTPUT-SCHEMA.md\nTRACEABILITY-RULES.md\n```\n\nSuccess condition:\n\nA product brief and selected template produce a complete `UI-COMPONENTS.md`.\n\n## Milestone 5 — Pattern library\n\nBuild the most reused patterns:\n\n```text\nsidebar-navigation.md\ntop-navigation.md\nbottom-navigation.md\ndashboard-grid.md\ndata-table.md\ncard-grid.md\ncollection-page.md\ndetail-page.md\nform-page.md\nloading.md\nempty.md\nerror.md\n```\n\nSuccess condition:\n\nTemplates reference shared patterns instead of duplicating instructions.\n\n## Milestone 6 — Validation\n\nBuild:\n\n```text\nTEMPLATE-CHECKLIST.md\nOUTPUT-CHECKLIST.md\nCONTRADICTION-RULES.md\nCOMPLETION-SCORING.md\n```\n\nSuccess condition:\n\nThe system identifies missing and contradictory UI architecture decisions.\n\n## Milestone 7 — Extensions\n\nBuild:\n\n```text\nanalytics.md\ncollaboration.md\nrole-based-access.md\nonboarding.md\nbilling.md\n```\n\nSuccess condition:\n\nHybrid products can be modeled without creating excessive templates.\n\n## Milestone 8 — Agent skill\n\nPackage the complete system into the reusable skill structure.\n\n---\n\n# Minimum Viable System\n\nThe first useful version should contain:\n\n```text\nui-component-system/\n├── README.md\n├── TEMPLATE-SCHEMA.md\n├── TEMPLATE-SELECTOR.md\n├── GENERATION-WORKFLOW.md\n├── NORMALIZED-VALUES.md\n│\n├── templates/\n│   ├── base/\n│   │   └── base-ui-architecture.md\n│   ├── websites/\n│   │   └── marketing-website.md\n│   ├── web-apps/\n│   │   └── saas-dashboard.md\n│   ├── commerce/\n│   │   └── ecommerce-storefront.md\n│   └── mobile/\n│       └── mobile-utility.md\n│\n├── assets/\n│   └── UI-COMPONENTS.template.md\n│\n└── validation/\n    └── OUTPUT-CHECKLIST.md\n```\n\nThe MVP must be able to:\n\n```text\n1. Read a product brief or PRD.\n2. Select one of four templates.\n3. Explain the selection.\n4. Generate the page inventory.\n5. Choose the navigation architecture.\n6. Assign layouts to each page.\n7. Select component families.\n8. Define responsive rules.\n9. Define system states.\n10. Produce UI-COMPONENTS.md.\n```\n\nThe MVP should not include:\n\n* Dozens of specialized templates\n* React or framework-specific components\n* Visual design generation\n* Automatic frontend code generation\n* A graphical template browser\n* A template marketplace\n* Complex scoring algorithms\n* Product-specific templates\n\nBuild the structural decision system first. Expand templates and extensions only after testing reveals repeated architectural needs.\n", (Source: `Rebuilding Stage 4 commands skills.md`)

- [medium] "formatted_output": "# Skill — ui-blueprint-specification\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `ui-blueprint-specification` skill transforms Stage 4 UX requirements into implementation-ready UI blueprints without generating frontend code.\n\nIt defines:\n\n* pages\n* screens\n* layouts\n* components\n* navigation\n* user actions\n* forms\n* tables\n* cards\n* modals\n* drawers\n* loading states\n* empty states\n* error states\n* frontend build package inputs\n\nThis skill is the bridge between Stage 4 UX architecture and Stage 5 frontend implementation planning.\n\nIt consumes the selected Stage 4 design system and visual references from `design-system-foundation`. It applies those decisions per page instead of inventing a separate visual direction for each blueprint.\n\n---\n\n# Operating Rule\n\nDo not ask broad questions such as:\n\n```text\nWhat should this dashboard look like?\n```\n\nForce every launch-critical page through the page-definition matrix:\n\n```text\nPAGE\nPurpose\nPrimary User\nScreen Type\nLayout Type\nSections\nComponents\nActions\nData Needed\nStates\nValidation\nNavigation\n```\n\nThen force every launch-critical page through the visual spec matrix:\n\n```text\nVISUAL SPEC\nVisual Style\nDesign System Refs\nVisual Reference Refs\nDensity\nColor Direction\nTypography Feel\nComponent Style\nPrimary Visual Focus\nResponsive Behavior\nVisual Do Rules\nVisual Don't Rules\nReference Apps\nDesign System Alignment\nVisual Acceptance Criteria\nUser Approval Status\n```\n\n---\n\n# Controlled Choices\n\nScreen type options:\n\n```text\nDashboard\nList\nDetail View\nForm\nWizard\nSettings\nProfile\nAnalytics\nMessaging\nLanding Page\nHero Page\nMarketing Page\nOnboarding\nPricing\nAuthentication\nAdmin\nCheckout\nCustom\n```\n\nScreen/page type selection must be contextual.\n\nThese options are a controlled vocabulary, not a required checklist. Include only page or screen types justified by:\n\n* Stage 1 product category and MVP scope\n* Stage 1 workflows and feature structure\n* Stage 3 selected stack and architecture constraints\n* Stage 4 user journeys and launch-critical interactions\n* user roles, permissions, and navigation needs\n\nDo not add `Landing Page`, `Hero Page`, `Dashboard`, `Admin`, `Checkout`, `Authentication`, `Pricing`, or any other page type unless the product model requires it.\n\nFor each selected page type, record:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"page_name\": \"\",\n  \"screen_type\": \"\",\n  \"included_because\": [],\n  \"source_refs\": [],\n  \"excluded_page_types\": [\n    {\n      \"screen_type\": \"\",\n      \"reason\": \"\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nAsk the user only when a launch-critical page type is ambiguous. Otherwise infer the page type from upstream workflow, role, feature, and route evidence, and record the assumption.\n\nLayout type options:\n\n```text\nSidebar\nTop Navigation\nSplit View\nCard Grid\nTable\nMobile First\nFull Screen\nCustom\n```\n\nComponent options:\n\n```text\nCards\nCharts\nTables\nSearch\nFilters\nForms\nTabs\nModals\nDrawers\nNotifications\nFile Upload\nComments\nTimeline\nMaps\nCalendar\n```\n\nAction options:\n\n```text\nCreate\nRead\nUpdate\nDelete\nExport\nShare\nInvite\nApprove\nReject\nUpload\nDownload\n```\n\nVisual style options:\n\n```text\nMinimal\nEnterprise\nEditorial\nConsumer App\nSaaS Dashboard\nData Dense\nPlayful\nLuxury\nUtility\nCustom\n```\n\nDensity options:\n\n```text\nCompact\nBalanced\nSpacious\nData Dense\nMobile First\nCustom\n```\n\nComponent style options:\n\n```text\nFlat\nOutlined\nSoft Card\nHigh Contrast\nDense Utility\nMedia Rich\nCustom\n```\n\n---\n\n# Complete App Blueprint Markdown\n\nGenerate a readable complete app blueprint tree at:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-4/09-complete-app-blueprint.md\n```\n\nThe markdown tree must use this structure, adapted to the app being built. The example page names below are illustrative only; the generated tree must include the pages required by the actual product:\n\n```text\nComplete App Blueprint\n│\n├── Pages\n│   ├── Example Landing Page\n│   │   ├── Hero\n│   │   ├── Feature Preview\n│   │   ├── CTA\n│   │   └── Footer\n│   ├── Example Dashboard\n│   │   ├── Summary Cards\n│   │   ├── Activity Feed\n│   │   └── Task Table\n│\n├── Components\n│\n├── Shared Components\n│\n├── Navigation\n│\n├── Routes\n│\n├── Actions\n│\n├── States\n│\n├── Data Requirements\n", (Source: `Rebuilding Stage 4 commands skills.md`)
- [medium] "formatted_output": "# Skill — design-system-foundation\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `design-system-foundation` skill defines the shared visual system that all Stage 4 UI blueprints must follow.\n\nIt produces an implementation-ready design contract without generating frontend code.\n\nIt defines:\n\n* design system identity\n* color tokens\n* typography tokens\n* spacing scale\n* radius rules\n* elevation and shadow rules\n* icon rules\n* button styles\n* card styles\n* form styles\n* table styles\n* modal and drawer styles\n* navigation styles\n* responsive breakpoints\n* visual reference handling\n* design approval status\n\nThis skill turns page-level visual intent into a shared UI consistency foundation.\n\n---\n\n# Operating Rule\n\nDo not generate frontend code or mockups.\n\nDo not ask broad questions such as:\n\n```text\nWhat should the app look like?\n```\n\nUse structured choices and targeted confirmation questions to define a reusable design system.\n\n---\n\n# Visual Reference Selection\n\nUse the visual direction library as source material for structured design decisions, not as loose inspiration.\n\nRead first:\n\n```text\n.opencode/Skills/design-system-foundation/references/visual-direction-index.md\n```\n\nThen select the smallest useful reference set:\n\n* one primary visual reference\n* zero or one secondary visual reference as a modifier\n* rejected references when they were plausible but not suitable\n\nRead only the selected reference files after consulting the index.\n\nRecord why each selected reference fits the product category, primary users, launch-critical surfaces, density needs, accessibility constraints, and Stage 4 visual specs.\n\nReject references that conflict with:\n\n* launch-critical workflow clarity\n* required information density\n* accessibility or contrast needs\n* product trust requirements\n* implementation feasibility for Stage 5\n\nConvert selected references into design-system tokens and rules before UI blueprints apply them.\n\nThe traceability path is:\n\n```text\nvisual style reference -> design system -> UI blueprint visual spec -> Stage 5 ticket -> Stage 6 visual QA\n```\n\n---\n\n# Design System Matrix\n\nForce the shared app design system through this matrix:\n\n```text\nDESIGN SYSTEM\nProduct Visual Personality\nDesign Style\nColor System\nTypography System\nSpacing System\nRadius System\nElevation System\nIcon Style\nButton Rules\nCard Rules\nForm Rules\nTable Rules\nModal And Drawer Rules\nNavigation Rules\nResponsive Breakpoints\nVisual References\nPrimary Visual Reference\nSecondary Visual References\nRejected Visual References\nLiked Patterns\nDisliked Patterns\nAccessibility Constraints\nDesign Do Rules\nDesign Don't Rules\nDesign Approval Status\n```\n\n---\n\n# Inputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user_journeys\": {},\n  \"interaction_architecture\": {},\n  \"screen_system\": {},\n  \"accessibility_framework\": {},\n  \"ui_blueprints\": {},\n  \"visual_spec_inventory\": [],\n  \"existing_state\": {}\n}\n```\n\nRead and update shared UX state from:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Build-status/UX-state.json\n```\n\n---\n\n# Outputs\n\nWrite or update:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-4/08-design-system-foundation.json\n```\n\nThe output must include:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"stage\": \"Stage 4\",\n  \"status\": \"\",\n  \"design_system\": {\n    \"design_system_id\": \"\",\n    \"product_visual_personality\": \"\",\n    \"design_style\": \"\",\n    \"color_tokens\": {},\n    \"typography_tokens\": {},\n    \"spacing_scale\": {},\n    \"radius_rules\": {},\n    \"elevation_rules\": {},\n    \"icon_rules\": {},\n    \"component_style_rules\": {\n      \"buttons\": {},\n      \"links\": {},\n \"navigation\": {}\n    },\n    \"interactive_component_mapping\": {\n      \"primary_action\": \"Button.Primary\",\n      \"secondary_action\": \"Button.Secondary\",\n      \"destructive_action\": \"Button.Destructive\",\n      \"navigation_link\": \"Link.Navigation\",\n      \"menu_item\": \"Menu.Item\",\n      \"tab_item\": \"Tab.Item\"\n    },\n    \"interaction_state_rules\": {\n      \"hover\": {},\n      \"focus_visible\": {},\n      \"pressed\": {},\n      \"selected\": {},\n      \"disabled\": {},\n      \"loading\": {},\n      \"error\": {}\n    },\n    \"responsive_breakpoints\": {\n      \"desktop\": \"\",\n      \"tablet\": \"\",\n      \"mobile\": \"\",\n      \"collapse_rules\": [],\n      \"mobile_priority_content\": []\n    },\n    \"visual_references\": [],\n    \"visual_reference_selection\": {\n      \"primary_reference\": {\n        \"name\": \"\",\n        \"path\": \"\",\n        \"selected_because\": [],\n        \"applicable_surfaces\": [],\n        \"token_implications\": [],\n        \"component_implications\": [],\n        \"accessibility_risks\": []\n      },\n      \"secondary_references\": [],\n      \"rejected_references\": []\n    },\n    \"liked_patterns\": [],\n    \"disliked_patterns\": [],\n    \"accessibility_constraints\": [],\n    \"design_do_rules\": [],\n    \"design_dont_rules\": [],\n    \"design_approval_status\": \"unconfirmed\"\n  },\n  \"ui_blueprint_alignment\": [],\n  \"stage_5_handoff\": {}\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Responsibilities\n\nAsk the user to confirm or choose:\n\n* product visual personality\n* design style\n* color direction\n* typography feel\n* density and spacing\n* component style direction\n* button hierarchy and link, menu, tab, interactive card, and row-action treatment\n* destructive, disabled, loading, selected, pressed, hover, and focus-visible treatment\n* visual references\n* primary visual reference\n* secondary visual reference when needed\n* liked and disliked patterns\n* approval status for the shared design system\n\nAsk no more than 1-3 design-system questions at once.\n\nInfer low-risk defaults only when they A trivial page may rely on its interaction contract and inventories when the app route map already covers it.\n\n---\n\n# Visual Hierarchy Model\n\nEach page blueprint must preserve:\n\n```text\nPage\n├─ Section\n│  ├─ Component\n│  │  ├─ Interactive Element\n│  │  │  └─ Route, Action, Or No Navigation\n│  │  ├─ Data Source\n│  │  ├─ Validation\n│  │  └─ \"element_id\": \"UI-ELEMENT-001\",\n  \"element_type\": \"button | link | icon_button | menu_item | tab | toggle | checkbox | radio | select | text_input | search_input | file_upload | date_picker | \"route_id\": \"ROUTE-001\",\n  \"path\": \"\",\n  \"page_ref\": \"\",\n  \"page_name\": \"\",\n  \"screen_type\": \"\",\n  \"is_launch_critical\": false,\n  \"role_access\": [],\n \"owning_page_refs\": []\n}\n```\n\n# Page Interaction Contract\n\nCreate one compact contract for every page recorded in `page_inventory` or `ui_blueprints`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"page_ref\": \"\",\n  \"ui_blueprint_id\": \"UI-BLUEPRINT-001\",\n  \"route_id\": \"ROUTE-001\",\n  \"criticality\": \"launch_critical | standard | supporting | deferred\",\n  \"interactive_element_count\": 0,\n \"mermaid_map_required\": false\n}\n```\n\nApply deeper design-system, mobile, accessibility, state, and user-confirmation detail to launch-critical pages. Apply confirmation, success, failure, loading, permission-denied, undo, and recovery detail to destructive, security-sensitive, payment, admin, permission-sensitive, and mutation actions.\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Responsibilities\n\nAsk the user to confirm or choose:\n\n* screen type\n* layout type\n* sections\n* components\n* user actions\n* required states\n* shared components\n* route and navigation expectations\n* visual style\n* density\n* color direction\n* typography feel\n* component style\n* primary visual focus\n* visual do and don't rules\n* visual acceptance criteria\n* user approval status\n\nInfer the full interactive element inventory before asking. - [medium] "formatted_output": "# UI-COMPONENT.md System Build Plan\n\n## 1. System Goal\n\nBuild a reusable system that generates a project-specific `UI-COMPONENTS.md` file from a selected UI architecture template.\n\nThe system should help define:\n\n* Application navigation\n* Application shell\n* Page hierarchy\n* Page layouts\n* Grid, table, list, and card usage\n* Component families\n* Interaction patterns\n* Responsive behavior\n* Loading, empty, error, and permission states\n* Accessibility expectations\n\nThe system should work independently from visual design styles.\n\nExample:\n\n```yaml\nui_architecture_template: saas-dashboard\nvisual_design_template: neobrutalism\n```\n\nThe UI architecture template determines structure and behavior.\n\nThe design template determines colors, typography, borders, shadows, and visual styling.\n\n---\n\n# 2. Final System Shape\n\nThe completed system should contain five major parts:\n\n```text\nUI-COMPONENT.md System\n├── Template schema\n├── UI architecture templates\n├── Template selector\n├── Project file generator\n└── Validation system\n```\n\nRecommended directory structure:\n\n```text\nui-component-system/\n├── README.md\n├── TEMPLATE-SCHEMA.md\n├── TEMPLATE-SELECTOR.md\n├── GENERATION-WORKFLOW.md\n├── OUTPUT-SCHEMA.md\n├── NORMALIZED-VALUES.md\n│\n├── templates/\n│   ├── base/\n│   │   └── base-ui-architecture.md\n│   ├── websites/\n│   ├── web-apps/\n│   ├── commerce/\n│   └── mobile/\n│\n├── patterns/\n│   ├── navigation/\n│   ├── layouts/\n│   ├── pages/\n│   ├── components/\n│   ├── interactions/\n│   └── states/\n│\n├── extensions/\n│   ├── analytics.md\n│   ├── collaboration.md\n│   ├── role-based-access.md\n│   └── onboarding.md\n│\n├── assets/\n│   └── UI-COMPONENTS.template.md\n│\n├── validation/\n│   ├── TEMPLATE-CHECKLIST.md\n│   ├── OUTPUT-CHECKLIST.md\n│   └── CONTRADICTION-RULES.md\n│\n└── tests/\n    ├── test-projects/\n    ├── expected-outputs/\n    └── TEST-RESULTS.md\n```\n\n---\n\n# Phase 1 — Define the System Boundaries\n\n## Step 1. Define what `UI-COMPONENTS.md` controls\n\nCreate a document that explicitly defines the file’s responsibilities.\n\nThe file should control:\n\n```yaml\nui_components_responsibilities:\n  - information-architecture\n  - application-navigation\n  - application-shell\n  - page-inventory\n  - page-archetypes\n  - page-layouts\n  - component-selection\n  - responsive-behavior\n  - interaction-patterns\n  - system-states\n  - accessibility-structure\n```\n\nThe file should not control:\n\n```yaml\nexcluded_responsibilities:\n  - final-color-palette\n  - typography-branding\n  - logo-treatment\n  - illustration-style\n  - backend-architecture\n  - database-schema\n  - API-design\n  - feature-requirements\n```\n\n## Step 2. Define the relationship with other project files\n\nCreate a clear document ownership map.\n\n```yaml\nproject_files:\n  PRD.md:\n    defines: product-requirements\n\n  USER-FLOWS.md:\n    defines: user-task-sequences\n\n  UI-COMPONENTS.md:\n    defines: interface-structure-and-behavior\n\n  DESIGN.md:\n    defines: visual-design-language\n\n  TECH-STACK.md:\n    defines: implementation-technology\n```\n\n## Step 3. Define the system terminology\n\nStandardize terms early.\n\nUse:\n\n```yaml\nterminology:\n  ui_template: A reusable structural architecture\n  page_archetype: A reusable page type\n  layout_pattern: A method of arranging page content\n  component_family: A group of related reusable components\n  extension: An optional capability added to a base template\n  project_output: The generated UI-COMPONENTS.md file\n  override: A project-specific replacement for a template default\n```\n\n## Phase 1 deliverables\n\n```text\nREADME.md\nDOCUMENT-BOUNDARIES.md\nTERMINOLOGY.md\n```\n\n---\n\n# Phase 2 — Build the Universal Template Schema\n\n## Step 4. Create `TEMPLATE-SCHEMA.md`\n\nEvery UI architecture template must use the same structure.\n\nRequired template sections:\n\n```text\n1. Template identity\n2. Product characteristics\n3. Structural defaults\n4. Information architecture\n5. Navigation architecture\n6. Application shell\n7. Page archetypes\n8. Page composition patterns\n9. Layout rules\n10. Component families\n11. Interaction patterns\n12. Responsive strategy\n13. System states\n14. Accessibility requirements\n15. Adaptation rules\n16. Output instructions\n```\n\n## Step 5. Define template metadata\n\nUse a standard frontmatter block.\n\n```yaml\n---\ntemplate_id: saas-dashboard\ntemplate_name: SaaS Dashboard\ncategory: web-app\nversion: 1.0.0\nstatus: stable\n", (Source: `Rebuilding Stage 4 commands skills.md`)

Build `mobile-utility.md`\n\nPrimary focus:\n\n* Short repeated workflows\n* Bottom navigation\n* One-handed interaction\n* Bottom sheets\n* Device permissions\n* Offline handling\n* Interrupted-session recovery\n* Large touch targets\n\nRequired page archetypes:\n\n```yaml\nrequired:\n  - mobile-home\n  - primary-task\n  - history-or-saved-items\n  - settings\n\nconditional:\n  - onboarding\n  - permissions\n  - account\n```\n\n## Phase 4 deliverables\n\n```text\ntemplates/websites/marketing-website.md\ntemplates/web-apps/saas-dashboard.md\ntemplates/commerce/ecommerce-storefront.md\ntemplates/mobile/mobile-utility.md\n```\n\n---\n\n# Phase 5 — Build the Pattern Library\n\nTemplates should reference shared patterns instead of repeating large blocks.\n\n## Step 15. Create navigation patterns\n\n```text\npatterns/navigation/\n├── top-navigation.md\n├── sidebar-navigation.md\n├── bottom-navigation.md\n├── navigation-drawer.md\n├── tabs.md\n└── breadcrumbs.md\n```\n\nEach navigation pattern should define:\n\n```yaml\npattern:\n  purpose:\n  use_when: []\n  avoid_when: []\n  anatomy: []\n  desktop_behavior:\n  tablet_behavior:\n  mobile_behavior:\n  accessibility:\n```\n\n## Step 16. Create layout patterns\n\n```text\npatterns/layouts/\n├── dashboard-grid.md\n├── card-grid.md\n├── data-table.md\n├── content-list.md\n├── master-detail.md\n├── split-pane.md\n├── form-layout.md\n└── settings-layout.md\n```\n\n## Step 17. Create page patterns\n\n```text\npatterns/pages/\n├── dashboard-page.md\n├── collection-page.md\n├── detail-page.md\n├── form-page.md\n├── settings-page.md\n├── search-results-page.md\n├── authentication-page.md\n└── onboarding-page.md\n```\n\n## Step 18. Create interaction patterns\n\n```text\npatterns/interactions/\n├── search.md\n├── filtering.md\n├── sorting.md\n├── bulk-actions.md\n├── creation.md\n├── editing.md\n├── deletion.md\n├── notifications.md\n└── permissions.md\n```\n\n## Step 19. Create state patterns\n\n```text\npatterns/states/\n├── loading.md\n├── empty.md\n├── error.md\n├── success.md\n├── offline.md\n└── permission-denied.md\n```\n\n## Phase 5 deliverables\n\nA complete reusable pattern library referenced by all templates.\n\n---\n\n# Phase 6 — Build the Template Selector\n\n## Step 20. Create the selector inputs\n\nThe selector should evaluate:\n\n```yaml\nselection_inputs:\n  product_category:\n  primary_platform:\n  primary_user_behavior:\n  dominant_workflow:\n  content_type:\n  information_density:\n  comparison_needs:\n  collaboration_level:\n  transaction_model:\n  session_frequency:\n```\n\n## Step 21. Create the selection questions\n\nUse a short structured questionnaire.\n\n```text\n1. What is the product’s primary purpose?\n2. What action do users perform most often?\n3. What type of content or records do users manage?\n4. Do users compare many items or values?\n5. Is the experience task-first or content-first?\n6. Is collaboration central to the product?\n7. Is the primary experience desktop or mobile?\n8. Does the system include purchasing or transactions?\n```\n\n## Step 22. Build the selection matrix\n\n```yaml\nselection_rules:\n  - condition:\n      purpose: promotion\n      experience: content-first\n    template: marketing-website\n\n  - condition:\n      purpose: recurring-business-workflows\n      platform: desktop-web\n    template: saas-dashboard\n\n  - condition:\n      purpose: direct-product-purchasing\n      transaction_model: seller-to-customer\n    template: ecommerce-storefront\n\n  - condition:\n      purpose: focused-repeated-task\n      platform: mobile\n    template: mobile-utility\n```\n\n## Step 23. Define the selector output\n\n```yaml\ntemplate_selection:\n  primary_template: saas-dashboard\n  confidence: high\n\n  alternative_templates:\n    - internal-admin-tool\n\n  recommended_extensions:\n    - analytics\n    - role-based-access\n\n  reasons:\n    - recurring-workflows\n    - desktop-first\n    - structured-record-management\n\n  unresolved_questions: []\n```\n\n## Phase 6 deliverables\n\n```text\nTEMPLATE-SELECTOR.md\nSELECTION-MATRIX.md\nSELECTION-QUESTIONS.md\n```\n\n---\n\n# Phase 7 — Build Template Extensions\n\nExtensions add capabilities without creating a completely new template.\n\n## Step 24. Define the extension schema\n\n```yaml\nextension:\n  id:\n  name:\n  version:\n  compatible_with: []\n  description:\n\nadds:\n  pages: []\n  components: []\n  interactions: []\n  states: []\n\nmodifies:\n  navigation: []\n  layouts: []\n  responsive_behavior: []\n\nrequires:\n  product_conditions: []\n```\n\n## Step 25. Build initial extensions\n\nStart with:\n\n```text\nextensions/\n├── analytics.md\n├── collaboration.md\n├── role-based-access.md\n├── onboarding.md\n├── billing.md\n├── messaging.md\n└── file-management.md\n```\n\n## Step 26. Define composition rules\n\nExample:\n\n```yaml\nui_architecture:\n  primary_template: saas-dashboard\n\n  extensions:\n    - analytics\n    - role-based-access\n    - collaboration\n```\n\n## Step 27. Define override precedence\n\n```yaml\nprecedence:\n  1: project-specific-requirements\n  2: explicit-project-overrides\n  3: selected-extensions\n  4: primary-template\n  5: base-template\n```\n\n## Phase 7 deliverables\n\n```text\nEXTENSION-SCHEMA.md\nTEMPLATE-COMPOSITION.md\nPRECEDENCE-RULES.md\nextensions/*.md\n```\n\n---\n\n# Phase 8 — Build the Project Generator\n\n## Step 28. Define generator inputs\n\n```yaml\ngenerator_inputs:\n  required:\n    - product-description-or-PRD\n    - selected-template\n\n  recommended:\n    - user-roles\n    - feature-list\n    - user-flows\n    - platform-targets\n\n  optional:\n    - selected-extensions\n    - design-template\n    - technical-constraints\n    - existing-components\n```\n\n## Step 29. Build the generation workflow\n\nThe generator should follow this sequence:\n\n```text\n1. Read the available product documentation.\n2. Extract the product purpose.\n3. Identify user roles.\n4. Identify primary workflows.\n5. Identify major product objects.\n6. Identify comparison-heavy tasks.\n7. Identify content-heavy tasks.\n8. Select or confirm the primary template.\n9. Select relevant extensions.\n10. Remove irrelevant template defaults.\n11. Define the application shell.\n12. Define the navigation architecture.\n13. Generate the page inventory.\n14. Assign a page archetype to every page.\n15. Select a layout pattern for every page.\n16. Select required component families.\n17. Define responsive transformations.\n18. Define system states.\n19. Define accessibility requirements.\n20. Record overrides and deviations.\n21. Generate `UI-COMPONENTS.md`.\n```\n\n## Step 30. Define the generated file structure\n\n```text\nUI-COMPONENTS.md\n├── Template metadata\n├── Product interface summary\n├── User roles\n├── Primary workflows\n├── Information architecture\n├── Navigation architecture\n├── Application shell\n├── Page inventory\n├── Page specifications\n├── Layout decisions\n├── Component inventory\n├── Interaction rules\n├── Responsive strategy\n├── System states\n├── Accessibility requirements\n", (Source: `Rebuilding Stage 4 commands skills.md`)

Define rule priority levels\n\nEach recommendation should be labeled as one of the following:\n\n```yaml\nrule_levels:\n  required:\n    meaning: Normally necessary for this archetype\n\n  recommended:\n    meaning: Default unless the project provides a reason to change it\n\n  conditional:\n    meaning: Only apply when a specific product condition exists\n\n  prohibited:\n    meaning: Normally incompatible with the archetype\n```\n\n## Step 7. Define normalized values\n\nCreate `NORMALIZED-VALUES.md`.\n\nThis prevents templates from using different names for the same pattern.\n\n### Navigation values\n\n```yaml\nnavigation_patterns:\n  - top-navigation\n  - sidebar-navigation\n  - bottom-navigation\n  - navigation-drawer\n  - split-navigation\n  - contextual-navigation\n  - tab-navigation\n```\n\n### Layout values\n\n```yaml\nlayout_patterns:\n  - single-column\n  - two-column\n  - responsive-grid\n  - dashboard-grid\n  - card-grid\n  - data-table\n  - content-list\n  - master-detail\n  - split-pane\n  - form-layout\n  - settings-layout\n```\n\n### Page archetypes\n\n```yaml\npage_archetypes:\n  - dashboard\n  - collection\n  - detail\n  - create-edit\n  - settings\n  - search-results\n  - authentication\n  - onboarding\n  - profile\n  - checkout\n  - messaging\n  - analytics\n```\n\n## Phase 2 deliverables\n\n```text\nTEMPLATE-SCHEMA.md\nNORMALIZED-VALUES.md\ntemplates/base/base-ui-architecture.md\n```\n\n---\n\n# Phase 3 — Build the Base UI Architecture Template\n\n## Step 8. Create the universal base template\n\nThe base template should contain rules shared by all interface types.\n\nIt should define:\n\n* Every page must have a purpose.\n* Every page must have a primary user goal.\n* Every page must declare a page archetype.\n* Every data region must define system states.\n* Every page must define responsive behavior.\n* Every navigation destination must map to a real page.\n* Every major component must have a clear responsibility.\n* Every primary action must be identifiable.\n* Every interactive component must define keyboard and touch behavior.\n\n## Step 9. Create the base page specification\n\nUse a common page schema.\n\n```yaml\npage:\n  id:\n  name:\n  route:\n  archetype:\n  purpose:\n  primary_user:\n  primary_goal:\n  entry_points: []\n  exit_points: []\n\nnavigation:\n  parent:\n  primary_location:\n  breadcrumbs: []\n  tabs: []\n\nheader:\n  title:\n  description:\n  primary_action:\n  secondary_actions: []\n\nlayout:\n  pattern:\n  content_width:\n  columns:\n  regions: []\n\ncomponents: []\n\nstates:\n  loading:\n  empty:\n  error:\n  populated:\n  permission_denied:\n\nresponsive:\n  desktop:\n  tablet:\n  mobile:\n\naccessibility:\n  landmarks:\n  heading_order:\n  keyboard_flow:\n  focus_behavior:\n```\n\n## Step 10. Create the base component specification\n\n```yaml\ncomponent:\n  id:\n  name:\n  category:\n  purpose:\n  reuse_level:\n  used_on: []\n\nanatomy: []\n\nvariants: []\n\nstates:\n  - default\n  - hover\n  - focus\n  - active\n  - disabled\n  - loading\n  - error\n\nbehavior:\n  click:\n  keyboard:\n  touch:\n  responsive:\n\naccessibility:\n  semantic_role:\n  keyboard_support:\n  screen_reader_label:\n  focus_management:\n```\n\n## Phase 3 deliverables\n\n```text\ntemplates/base/base-ui-architecture.md\nassets/UI-COMPONENTS.template.md\n```\n\n---\n\n# Phase 4 — Build the First Template Set\n\nStart with four templates that are structurally different.\n\n## Step 11. Build `marketing-website.md`\n\nPrimary focus:\n\n* Top navigation\n* Hero section\n* Conversion paths\n* Feature sections\n* Social proof\n* Pricing\n* FAQ\n* Footer\n* Responsive content sections\n\nRequired page archetypes:\n\n```yaml\nrequired:\n  - landing-page\n  - product-or-service-page\n  - contact-or-conversion-page\n\nconditional:\n  - pricing\n  - case-studies\n  - blog\n  - documentation\n```\n\n## Step 12. Build `saas-dashboard.md`\n\nPrimary focus:\n\n* Persistent sidebar\n* Utility top bar\n* Dashboard\n* Record collections\n* Detail pages\n* Forms\n* Settings\n* Search and filtering\n* Tables and operational data\n\nRequired page archetypes:\n\n```yaml\nrequired:\n  - dashboard\n  - collection\n  - detail\n  - create-edit\n  - settings\n\nconditional:\n  - analytics\n  - billing\n  - team-management\n  - integrations\n```\n\n## Step 13. Build `ecommerce-storefront.md`\n\nPrimary focus:\n\n* Product discovery\n* Category navigation\n* Product grids\n* Product detail\n* Search\n* Cart\n* Checkout\n* Account\n* Order history\n\nRequired page archetypes:\n\n```yaml\nrequired:\n  - storefront-home\n", (Source: `Rebuilding Stage 4 commands skills.md`)
