- [medium] "formatted_output": "# Skill — ui-blueprint-specification\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `ui-blueprint-specification` skill transforms Stage 4 UX requirements into implementation-ready UI blueprints without generating frontend code.\n\nIt defines:\n\n* pages\n* screens\n* layouts\n* components\n* navigation\n* user actions\n* forms\n* tables\n* cards\n* modals\n* drawers\n* loading states\n* empty states\n* error states\n* frontend build package inputs\n\nThis skill is the bridge between Stage 4 UX architecture and Stage 5 frontend implementation planning.\n\nIt consumes the selected Stage 4 design system and visual references from `design-system-foundation`. It applies those decisions per page instead of inventing a separate visual direction for each blueprint.\n\n---\n\n# Operating Rule\n\nDo not ask broad questions such as:\n\n```text\nWhat should this dashboard look like?\n```\n\nForce every launch-critical page through the page-definition matrix:\n\n```text\nPAGE\nPurpose\nPrimary User\nScreen Type\nLayout Type\nSections\nComponents\nActions\nData Needed\nStates\nValidation\nNavigation\n```\n\nThen force every launch-critical page through the visual spec matrix:\n\n```text\nVISUAL SPEC\nVisual Style\nDesign System Refs\nVisual Reference Refs\nDensity\nColor Direction\nTypography Feel\nComponent Style\nPrimary Visual Focus\nResponsive Behavior\nVisual Do Rules\nVisual Don't Rules\nReference Apps\nDesign System Alignment\nVisual Acceptance Criteria\nUser Approval Status\n```\n\n---\n\n# Controlled Choices\n\nScreen type options:\n\n```text\nDashboard\nList\nDetail View\nForm\nWizard\nSettings\nProfile\nAnalytics\nMessaging\nLanding Page\nHero Page\nMarketing Page\nOnboarding\nPricing\nAuthentication\nAdmin\nCheckout\nCustom\n```\n\nScreen/page type selection must be contextual.\n\nThese options are a controlled vocabulary, not a required checklist. Include only page or screen types justified by:\n\n* Stage 1 product category and MVP scope\n* Stage 1 workflows and feature structure\n* Stage 3 selected stack and architecture constraints\n* Stage 4 user journeys and launch-critical interactions\n* user roles, permissions, and navigation needs\n\nDo not add `Landing Page`, `Hero Page`, `Dashboard`, `Admin`, `Checkout`, `Authentication`, `Pricing`, or any other page type unless the product model requires it.\n\nFor each selected page type, record:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"page_name\": \"\",\n  \"screen_type\": \"\",\n  \"included_because\": [],\n  \"source_refs\": [],\n  \"excluded_page_types\": [\n    {\n      \"screen_type\": \"\",\n      \"reason\": \"\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nAsk the user only when a launch-critical page type is ambiguous. Otherwise infer the page type from upstream workflow, role, feature, and route evidence, and record the assumption.\n\nLayout type options:\n\n```text\nSidebar\nTop Navigation\nSplit View\nCard Grid\nTable\nMobile First\nFull Screen\nCustom\n```\n\nComponent options:\n\n```text\nCards\nCharts\nTables\nSearch\nFilters\nForms\nTabs\nModals\nDrawers\nNotifications\nFile Upload\nComments\nTimeline\nMaps\nCalendar\n```\n\nAction options:\n\n```text\nCreate\nRead\nUpdate\nDelete\nExport\nShare\nInvite\nApprove\nReject\nUpload\nDownload\n```\n\nVisual style options:\n\n```text\nMinimal\nEnterprise\nEditorial\nConsumer App\nSaaS Dashboard\nData Dense\nPlayful\nLuxury\nUtility\nCustom\n```\n\nDensity options:\n\n```text\nCompact\nBalanced\nSpacious\nData Dense\nMobile First\nCustom\n```\n\nComponent style options:\n\n```text\nFlat\nOutlined\nSoft Card\nHigh Contrast\nDense Utility\nMedia Rich\nCustom\n```\n\n---\n\n# Complete App Blueprint Markdown\n\nGenerate a readable complete app blueprint tree at:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-4/09-complete-app-blueprint.md\n```\n\nThe markdown tree must use this structure, adapted to the app being built. The example page names below are illustrative only; the generated tree must include the pages required by the actual product:\n\n```text\nComplete App Blueprint\n│\n├── Pages\n│   ├── Example Landing Page\n│   │   ├── Hero\n│   │   ├── Feature Preview\n│   │   ├── CTA\n│   │   └── Footer\n│   ├── Example Dashboard\n│   │   ├── Summary Cards\n│   │   ├── Activity Feed\n│   │   └── Task Table\n│\n├── Components\n│\n├── Shared Components\n│\n├── Navigation\n│\n├── Routes\n│\n├── Actions\n│\n├── States\n│\n├── Data Requirements\n│\n└── Frontend Build Package\n```\n\nEvery launch-critical page in the markdown tree must map to a `ui_blueprint_id` and include its sections, components, primary actions, route, states, and data requirements.\n\nThe complete app blueprint must also include:\n\n* one compact Mermaid app route map covering every created page\n* page-level Mermaid interaction maps for launch-critical or complex pages\n* critical workflow Mermaid maps that include success, failure, and recovery branches\n* destructive or mutation Mermaid maps that include confirmation and result states\n\nRequire a page-level Mermaid map when a page has multiple interaction branches, destructive or mutation actions, modal or drawer flows, or complex routing. A trivial page may rely on its interaction contract and inventories when the app route map already covers it.\n\n---\n\n# Visual Hierarchy Model\n\nEach page blueprint must preserve:\n\n```text\nPage\n├─ Section\n│  ├─ Component\n│  │  ├─ Interactive Element\n│  │  │  └─ Route, Action, Or No Navigation\n│  │  ├─ Data Source\n│  │  ├─ Validation\n│  │  └─ States\n```\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Element Schema\n\nEvery interactive element on a page (button, link, icon button, menu item, tab, input, etc.) must be enumerated with:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"element_id\": \"UI-ELEMENT-001\",\n  \"element_type\": \"button | link | icon_button | menu_item | tab | toggle | checkbox | radio | select | text_input | search_input | file_upload | date_picker | breadcrumb | pagination | clickable_card | clickable_row | disclosure\",\n  \"label\": \"\",\n  \"accessible_name\": \"\",\n  \"icon\": \"\",\n  \"owning_page_ref\": \"\",\n  \"owning_section_ref\": \"\",\n  \"owning_component_ref\": \"\",\n  \"route_id\": \"\",\n  \"route_target\": \"\",\n  \"route_type\": \"internal_page | external_url | modal | drawer | anchored_section | file_download | api_action | state_transition | no_navigation\",\n  \"action_id\": \"ACTION-001\",\n  \"behavior\": \"navigate | submit | open_modal | open_drawer | toggle | trigger_action | open_link | download | call_api | scroll_to | no_navigation\",\n  \"behavior_target\": \"\",\n  \"design_system_component\": \"\",\n  \"states\": {\n    \"default\": {},\n    \"loading\": {},\n    \"disabled\": {},\n    \"active\": {},\n    \"hover\": {}\n  },\n  \"permission_required\": \"\",\n  \"permission_denied_behavior\": \"\",\n  \"confirmation_required\": false,\n  \"responsive_behavior\": {},\n  \"accessibility_behavior\": {},\n  \"analytics_event\": \"\",\n  \"source_trace\": []\n}\n```\n\n# Action Inventory Schema\n\nEvery action across all pages must be recorded in a global action inventory:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"action_id\": \"ACTION-001\",\n  \"name\": \"\",\n  \"element_type\": \"button | link | icon_button | menu_item | tab | toggle | checkbox | radio | select\",\n  \"label\": \"\",\n  \"route_target\": \"\",\n  \"behavior\": \"navigate | submit | open_modal | open_drawer | toggle | trigger_action | open_link | download | call_api | scroll_to\",\n  \"behavior_target\": \"\",\n  \"owning_page_refs\": [],\n  \"owning_component_refs\": [],\n  \"triggering_element_refs\": [],\n  \"permission_required\": \"\",\n  \"confirmation_required\": false,\n  \"success_destination\": \"\",\n  \"failure_destination\": \"\",\n  \"loading_state\": \"\",\n  \"empty_state\": \"\",\n  \"permission_denied_behavior\": \"\",\n  \"undo_or_recovery_path\": \"\",\n  \"states\": {},\n  \"analytics_event\": \"\",\n  \"source_trace\": []\n}\n```\n\n# Route Inventory Schema\n\nEvery route across all pages must be recorded in a global route inventory:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"route_id\": \"ROUTE-001\",\n  \"path\": \"\",\n  \"page_ref\": \"\",\n  \"page_name\": \"\",\n  \"screen_type\": \"\",\n  \"is_launch_critical\": false,\n  \"role_access\": [],\n  \"owning_journey_ids\": [],\n  \"related_routes\": [],\n  \"source_trace\": []\n}\n```\n\n# Navigation Inventory Schema\n\nEvery navigation item across the app must be recorded:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"nav_item_id\": \"\",\n  \"label\": \"\",\n  \"route_target\": \"\",\n  \"icon\": \"\",\n  \"order\": 0,\n  \"group\": \"\",\n  \"permission_required\": \"\",\n  \"children\": [],\n  \"owning_page_refs\": []\n}\n```\n\n# Page Interaction Contract\n\nCreate one compact contract for every page recorded in `page_inventory` or `ui_blueprints`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"page_ref\": \"\",\n  \"ui_blueprint_id\": \"UI-BLUEPRINT-001\",\n  \"route_id\": \"ROUTE-001\",\n  \"criticality\": \"launch_critical | standard | supporting | deferred\",\n  \"interactive_element_count\": 0,\n  \"interactive_element_refs\": [],\n  \"unresolved_element_refs\": [],\n  \"assumptions\": [],\n  \"approval_status\": \"approved | assumed_low_risk | needs_user_review | blocked\",\n  \"mermaid_map_required\": false\n}\n```\n\nApply deeper design-system, mobile, accessibility, state, and user-confirmation detail to launch-critical pages. Apply confirmation, success, failure, loading, permission-denied, undo, and recovery detail to destructive, security-sensitive, payment, admin, permission-sensitive, and mutation actions.\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Responsibilities\n\nAsk the user to confirm or choose:\n\n* screen type\n* layout type\n* sections\n* components\n* user actions\n* required states\n* shared components\n* route and navigation expectations\n* visual style\n* density\n* color direction\n* typography feel\n* component style\n* primary visual focus\n* visual do and don't rules\n* visual acceptance criteria\n* user approval status\n\nInfer the full interactive element inventory before asking. Present the proposal and ask the user to approve, remove, rename, reroute, or add elements only when the decision is material. Do not ask the broad question \"what interactive elements should be on this page?\".\n\nAsk no more than 1-3 page-definition questions at once.\n\nInfer common UI patterns when strongly implied by screen type and workflow, but record assumptions in:\n\n```text\ninteractive_guidance.assumptions_made\n```\n\nPause for user input when:\n\n* a launch-critical page lacks purpose\n* a screen type cannot be inferred\n* layout choice materially affects navigation or implementation\n* required components or actions are ambiguous\n* required states are missing for a launch-critical interaction\n* visual style, density, or primary visual focus is missing for a launch-critical page\n* the user has not approved the visual spec for a launch-critical page\n\n---\n\n# Inputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user_journeys\": {},\n  \"interaction_architecture\": {},\n  \"screen_system\": {},\n  \"feature_behaviors\": {},\n  \"state_transition_map\": {},\n  \"accessibility_framework\": {},\n  \"design_system_foundation\": {},\n  \"visual_reference_selection\": {},\n  \"existing_state\": {}\n}\n```\n\nRead and update shared UX state from:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Build-status/UX-state.json\n```\n\n---\n\n# Outputs\n\nWrite or update:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-4/07-ui-blueprint-specification.json\n```\n\nThe output must include:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"stage\": \"Stage 4\",\n  \"status\": \"\",\n  \"ui_blueprints\": [],\n  \"page_inventory\": [],\n  \"interaction_contracts\": [],\n  \"interactive_element_inventory\": [],\n  \"page_type_selection_rationale\": [],\n  \"component_inventory\": [],\n  \"visual_spec_inventory\": [],\n  \"visual_reference_selection\": {},\n  \"shared_components\": [],\n  \"navigation_inventory\": [],\n  \"route_inventory\": [],\n  \"state_inventory\": [],\n  \"action_inventory\": [],\n  \"frontend_build_package\": {\n    \"page_count\": 0,\n    \"component_count\": \"validation_method\": \"\"\n}\n```\n\n## UI Blueprint Contract\n\nThe UI blueprint layer must convert screens and interaction requirements into implementation-ready UI specifications without producing frontend code.\n\nEach page or screen must be defined through a visual page-definition matrix:\n\n```text\nPAGE:\nPurpose:\nPrimary User:\nScreen Type:\nLayout Type:\nSections:\nComponents:\nActions:\nData Needed:\nStates:\nValidation:\nNavigation:\n```\n\nThe skill must avoid vague prompts such as:\n\n```text\nWhat should this dashboard look like?\n```\n\nInstead, it must force controlled choices.\n\nScreen type options:\n\n```text\n1. Dashboard\n2. List\n3. Detail View\n4. Form\n5. Wizard\n6. Settings\n7. Profile\n8. Analytics\n9. Messaging\n10. Landing Page\n11. Hero Page\n12. Marketing Page\n13. Onboarding\n14. Pricing\n15. Authentication\n16. Admin\n17. Checkout\n18. Custom\n```\n\nScreen/page type selection must be contextual.\n\nThese options are a controlled vocabulary, not a required checklist. Stage 4 must only include page or screen types that are justified by:\n\n* Stage 1 product category and MVP scope\n* Stage 1 workflows and feature structure\n* Stage 3 selected stack and architecture constraints\n* Stage 4 user journeys and launch-critical interactions\n* user roles, permissions, and navigation needs\n\nDo not add `Landing Page`, `Hero Page`, `Dashboard`, `Admin`, `Checkout`, `Authentication`, `Pricing`, or any other page type unless the product model requires it.\n\nEach selected page type must record a rationale:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"page_name\": \"\",\n  \"screen_type\": \"\",\n  \"included_because\": [],\n  \"source_refs\": [],\n  \"excluded_page_types\": [\n    {\n      \"screen_type\": \"\",\n      \"reason\": \"\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nAsk the user only when a launch-critical page type is ambiguous. Otherwise infer the page type from upstream workflow, role, feature, and route evidence, and record the assumption.\n\nLayout type options:\n\n```text\n1. Sidebar\n2. Top Navigation\n3. Split View\n4. Card Grid\n5. Table\n6. Mobile First\n7. Full Screen\n8. must preserve this visual hierarchy:\n\n```text\nPage\n├─ Section\n│  ├─ Component\n│  │  ├─ Action\n│  │  ├─ Data Source\n│  │  ├─ Validation\n│  │  └─ States\n```\n\nBlueprint - [medium] "formatted_output": "# Orchestrated Skills\n\nRun Stage 4 skills in this order:\n\n```text\n1. user-journey-design\n2. interaction-architecture-design\n3. screen-system-design\n4. feature-behavior-specification\n5. state-transition-and-accessibility-design\n6. design-system-foundation\n7. ui-blueprint-specification\n8. ux-interaction-synthesis\n```\n\n---\n\n# Skill — user-journey-design\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `user-journey-design` skill defines the main user journeys and outcome paths.\n\nIt determines:\n\n* primary user journeys\n* secondary user journeys\n* entry points\n* success states\n* failure states\n* role-specific journey differences\n* MVP journey boundaries\n\n---\n\n# Core Responsibilities\n\n## Journey Mapping\n\nDefine:\n\n* user goals\n* journey start states\n* user actions\n* system responses\n* decision points\n* success outcomes\n* failure outcomes\n* recovery paths\n\n## Role and Persona Mapping\n\nMap journeys across:\n\n* primary users\n* secondary users\n* admins or operators\n* guest or unauthenticated users\n* permission-based user roles\n\n## Journey Risk Detection\n\nIdentify:\n\n* missing user goals\n* unclear success states\n* excessive friction\n* unsupported failure recovery\n* role conflicts\n* MVP journey gaps\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Responsibilities\n\nThis skill should guide the user only when journeys cannot be inferred safely.\n\nAsk targeted questions when any of these are unclear:\n\n* primary user goal\n* first action in the journey\n* successful end state\n* failure or recovery behavior\n* role-specific journey differences\n* whether a journey is MVP-critical or deferred\n\nInfer common journey defaults when the workflow and user profile make them obvious, but record the assumption in:\n\n```text\ninteractive_guidance.assumptions_made\n```\n\nPause for user input when a journey decision changes screens, permissions, feature behavior, or MVP scope.\n\n---\n\n# Inputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user_profiles\": {},\n  \"workflows\": {},\n  \"feature_structure\": {},\n  \"mvp_scope\": {},\n  \"existing_state\": {}\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Outputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user_journeys\": {},\n  \"journey_roles\": [],\n  \"entry_points\": [],\n  \"success_states\": [],\n  \"failure_states\": [],\n  \"journey_risks\": [],\n  \"open_questions\": []\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Shared State Updates\n\n```text\nuser_journeys\nux_decisions\nux_risks\nopen_questions\ninteractive_guidance\n```\n\n---\n\n# Skill — interaction-architecture-design\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `interaction-architecture-design` skill defines how users interact with product workflows and system responses.\n\nIt determines:\n\n* interaction patterns\n* navigation model\n* decision points\n* command flows\n* feedback patterns\n* error and recovery interactions\n* role-based interaction differences\n\n---\n\n# Core Responsibilities\n\n## Interaction Model\n\nDefine:\n\n* navigation paths\n* action patterns\n* confirmation patterns\n* feedback and notification behavior\n* user input patterns\n* system response patterns\n* recovery behavior\n\n## Interaction Constraints\n\nMap constraints from:\n\n* system topology\n* APIs\n* permissions\n* data ownership\n* asynchronous processing\n* security requirements\n\n## Interaction Risk Detection\n\nIdentify:\n\n* confusing flows\n* missing feedback\n* hidden system delays\n* unsafe destructive actions\n* permission ambiguity\n* unsupported recovery paths\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Responsibilities\n\nThis skill should guide the user through interaction decisions that materially affect workflow usability.\n\nAsk targeted questions when any of these are unclear:\n\n* navigation model\n* whether a user action needs confirmation\n* how async processing should be communicated\n* how errors or failed actions should be handled\n* whether actions are reversible\n* how users move between related workflows\n* how permission limits should appear to users\n\nInfer standard interaction defaults when risk is low, but record the assumption in:\n\n```text\ninteractive_guidance.assumptions_made\n```\n\nPause for user input when an interaction decision changes workflow completion, safety, permissions, or recovery.\n\n---\n\n# Inputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user_journeys\": {},\n  \"workflows\": {},\n  \"api_architecture\": {},\n  \"security_foundations\": {},\n  \"existing_state\": {}\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Outputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"interaction_architecture\": {},\n  \"navigation_model\": {},\n  \"interaction_patterns\": [],\n  \"feedback_patterns\": [],\n  \"recovery_patterns\": [],\n  \"interaction_risks\": []\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Shared State Updates\n\n```text\ninteraction_architecture\nux_decisions\nux_risks\ninteraction_tradeoffs\ninteractive_guidance\n```\n\n---\n\n# Skill — screen-system-design\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `screen-system-design` skill defines the screen architecture needed to support user journeys and interactions.\n\nIt determines:\n\n* screens\n* screen groups\n* layout responsibilities\n* information hierarchy\n* navigation structure\n* role-based screen access\n* MVP screen boundaries\n\n---\n\n# Core Responsibilities\n\n## Screen Architecture\n\nDefine:\n\n* required screens\n* screen purpose\n* screen inputs\n* screen outputs\n* screen-level user actions\n* screen data requirements\n* screen permissions\n* screen relationships\n\n## Screen System Consistency\n\nValidate:\n\n* screens map to journeys\n* screens support feature behavior\n* screen groups are coherent\n* navigation is complete\n* MVP screens are not over-scoped\n\n## Screen Risk Detection\n\nIdentify:\n\n* missing screens\n* redundant screens\n* unclear screen ownership\n* overloaded screens\n* role-based access confusion\n* unsupported workflow steps\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Responsibilities\n\nThis skill should guide the user through screen decisions that affect workflow completeness or interface consistency.\n\nAsk targeted questions when any of these are unclear:\n\n* whether a workflow step needs its own screen\n* whether admin/operator screens are required\n* which screens are MVP-critical\n* how role-based access changes screens\n* whether a screen should support creation, editing, review, or reporting\n* whether a dashboard, detail view, or list view is needed\n\nInfer standard screen patterns when the journey is simple and low-risk.\n\nRecord assumptions in:\n\n```text\ninteractive_guidance.assumptions_made\n```\n\nPause for user input when screen architecture affects journey completion, permissions, or Stage 5 implementation scope.\n\n---\n\n# {}\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Outputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"screen_system\": {},\n  \"screen_groups\": [],\n  \"screen_inventory\": [],\n  \"navigation_structure\": {},\n  \"screen_risks\": [],\n feature-behavior-specification\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `feature-behavior-specification` skill defines how product features behave in response to user actions and system conditions.\n\nIt determines:\n\n* feature behavior\n* user-triggered behavior\n* system-triggered behavior\n* validation rules\n* permission behavior\n* error behavior\n* empty, loading, success, and failure states\n\n---\n\n# Core Responsibilities\n\n## Behavior Specification\n\nDefine:\n\n* feature purpose\n* trigger actions\n* system responses\n* required inputs\n* expected outputs\n* validation rules\n* permission checks\n* error and recovery behavior\n\n## Behavior Consistency\n\nValidate:\n\n* feature behavior supports journeys\n* behavior aligns with APIs and data model\n* behavior respects permissions\n* behavior supports MVP scope\n* behavior exposes clear feedback\n\n## Behavior Risk Detection\n\nIdentify:\n\n* ambiguous feature behavior\n* missing validation rules\n* unsafe destructive behavior\n* unclear permissions\n* hidden async states\n* missing empty or error states\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Responsibilities\n\nThis skill should guide the user through feature behavior decisions that affect user trust, safety, and implementation clarity.\n\nAsk targeted questions when any of these are unclear:\n\n* what triggers a feature\n* what happens after a user action\n* what validation rules apply\n* what users can edit, delete, submit, approve, or cancel\n* how errors should be handled\n* whether actions are reversible\n* what states the feature must support\n\nInfer standard behavior only when feature purpose and workflow context are clear.\n\nRecord assumptions in:\n\n```text\ninteractive_guidance.assumptions_made\n```\n\nPause for user input when feature behavior affects safety, permissions, validation, or implementation scope.\n\n---\n\n# Inputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"feature_structure\": {},\n  \"user_journeys\": {},\n  \"interaction_architecture\": {},\n  \"screen_system\": {},\n  \"api_architecture\": {},\n  \"security_foundations\": {},\n  \"existing_state\": {}\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Outputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"feature_behaviors\": {},\n  \"behavior_rules\": [],\n  \"validation_rules\": [],\n  \"permission_behaviors\": [],\n  \"error_behaviors\": [],\n  \"behavior_risks\": []\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Shared State Updates\n\n```text\nfeature_behaviors\nux_decisions\nux_risks\ninteraction_tradeoffs\ninteractive_guidance\n```\n\n---\n\n# Skill — state-transition-and-accessibility-design\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `state-transition-and-accessibility-design` skill defines user-visible state transitions and accessibility foundations.\n\nIt determines:\n\n* workflow states\n* screen states\n* feature states\n* transition triggers\n* loading and async states\n* accessibility requirements\n* inclusive interaction constraints\n\n---\n\n# Core Responsibilities\n\n## State Transition Mapping\n\nDefine:\n\n* start states\n* intermediate states\n* success states\n* failure states\n* loading states\n* empty states\n* permission-denied states\n* transition triggers\n\n## Accessibility Framework\n\nDefine:\n\n* keyboard interaction requirements\n* screen reader expectations\n* focus management needs\n* contrast and readability needs\n* form accessibility requirements\n* error messaging accessibility\n* motion and animation constraints\n\n## State and Accessibility Risk Detection\n\nIdentify:\n\n* missing state transitions\n* unclear loading behavior\n* inaccessible interaction patterns\n* missing focus or keyboard behavior\n* unclear error messaging\n* visual-only feedback risks\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Responsibilities\n\nThis skill should guide the user through state and accessibility decisions that affect task completion and inclusive use.\n\nAsk targeted questions when any of these are unclear:\n\n* what states a workflow can enter\n* how users know something is processing\n* how users recover from failure\n* whether keyboard-only use is required\n* whether screen reader support is required\n* whether motion, timing, or contrast constraints matter\n* how permission-denied or unavailable states should behave\n\nInfer baseline accessibility requirements as required, not optional.\n\nRecord assumptions in:\n\n```text\ninteractive_guidance.assumptions_made\n```\n\nPause for user input when a state or accessibility decision affects core task completion or legal/compliance expectations.\n\n---\n\n# Inputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user_journeys\": {},\n  \"interaction_architecture\": {},\n  \"screen_system\": {},\n  \"feature_behaviors\": {},\n  \"security_foundations\": {},\n  \"existing_state\": {}\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Outputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"state_transition_map\": {},\n  \"workflow_states\": [],\n  \"screen_states\": [],\n  \"feature_states\": [],\n  \"accessibility_framework\": {},\n  \"accessibility_risks\": []\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Shared State Updates\n\n```text\nstate_transition_map\naccessibility_framework\nux_decisions\nux_risks\ninteractive_guidance\n```\n\n---\n\n# Skill — ui-blueprint-specification\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `ui-blueprint-specification` skill transforms UX requirements into implementation-ready UI blueprints without generating frontend code.\n\nIt defines:\n\n* pages\n* screens\n* layouts\n* components\n* navigation\n* user actions\n* states\n* forms\n* tables\n* cards\n* modals\n* drawers\n* empty states\n* loading states\n* error states\n* frontend build package inputs\n\nThis skill is the bridge between Stage 4 UX architecture and Stage 5 frontend implementation planning.\n\n---\n\n# Core Responsibilities\n\n## Page Definition Matrix\n\nForce each page or screen through a structured matrix:\n\n```text\nPAGE\nPurpose\nPrimary User\nScreen Type\nLayout Type\nSections\nComponents\nActions\nData Needed\nStates\nValidation\nNavigation\n```\n\nThe skill must ask controlled UI questions using screen type, layout type, component selection, and action mapping options instead of broad visual preference questions.\n\n## Visual Spec Matrix\n\nForce each launch-critical page or screen through a visual specification matrix:\n\n```text\nVISUAL SPEC\nVisual Style\nDensity\nColor Direction\nTypography Feel\nComponent Style\nPrimary Visual Focus\nResponsive Behavior\nVisual Do Rules\nVisual Don't Rules\nReference Apps\nVisual Acceptance Criteria\nUser Approval Status\n```\n\nThe visual spec matrix captures how the UI should visually feel and what the frontend builder must preserve. It must not generate frontend code or mockups.\n\n## Visual Hierarchy Modeling\n\nRepresent each page as:\n\n```text\nPage\n├─ Section\n│  ├─ Component\n│  │  ├─ Action\n│  │  ├─ Data Source\n│  │  ├─ Validation\n│  │  └─ States\n```\n\n## Frontend Build Package\n\nGenerate a frontend build package containing:\n\n* page inventory\n* component inventory\n* shared components\n* navigation inventory\n* route inventory\n* state inventory\n* action inventory\n* frontend tasks\n* recommended frontend skills\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Responsibilities\n\nAsk the user to confirm or choose:\n\n* screen type\n* layout type\n* sections\n* component selections\n* user actions\n* required states\n* shared components\n* route/navigation expectations\n* visual style\n* density\n* color direction\n* typography feel\n* component style\n* primary visual focus\n* visual do and don't rules\n* visual acceptance criteria\n* user approval status\n\nAsk no more than 1-3 page-definition questions at once.\n\nInfer common UI patterns when they are strongly implied by the screen type and workflow, but record them in:\n\n```text\ninteractive_guidance.assumptions_made\n```\n\nPause for user input when:\n\n* a launch-critical page lacks purpose\n* a screen type cannot be inferred\n* a layout choice materially affects navigation or implementation\n* required components or actions are ambiguous\n* required states are missing for a launch-critical interaction\n* visual style, density, or primary visual focus is missing for a launch-critical page\n* the user has not approved the visual spec for a launch-critical page\n\nUpdate:\n\n```text\ninteractive_guidance.open_questions\ninteractive_guidance.answered_questions\ninteractive_guidance.assumptions_made\ninteractive_guidance.blocked_decisions\ninteractive_guidance.ux_confidence_gaps\n```\n\n---\n\n# \"open_questions\": []\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n# Shared State Updates\n\n```text\nui_blueprints\nvisual_spec_inventory\nfrontend_build_package\nstage_5_handoff\nux_confidence_gaps\n```\n\n---\n\n# Skill — design-system-foundation\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `design-system-foundation` skill defines the shared design system that all Stage 4 UI blueprints must follow.\n\nIt produces an implementation-ready visual contract without generating frontend code.\n\nIt defines:\n\n* product visual personality\n", (Source: `Rebuilding Stage 4 commands skills.md`)

The command skills and final synthesis skills now reflect the same major gates, especially the Stage 1-4 decision brief approval flow.\n\nLatest check date: **2026-07-05**\n\nThe latest check also reviewed the new Stage 4 visual style reference workflow. The live skill layer now routes visual style references through:\n\n```text\ndesign-system-foundation\n-> ui-blueprint-specification\n-> ux-interaction-synthesis\n-> Stage 5 tickets and agent handoffs\n-> Stage 6 validation and visual QA\n-> Stage 7 launch readiness\n```\n\nThe major prior gaps have been addressed:\n\n- artifact evidence registry\n- stage contract profiles\n- schema validation expectations\n- Stage 2 evidence quality\n- Stage 7 deployment proof\n- Stage 8 feedback routing\n- complexity-based interactive guidance\n- risk acceptance ledger\n- cross-stage reference integrity\n- readiness failure revision loops\n- standardized `expected_artifacts`\n- Stage 1-4 `stage_decision_brief` approval gates\n- schema support for `stage_decision_brief`\n- visual direction index for design-system reference selection\n- `visual_reference_selection` and `visual_reference_refs`\n- visual reference compliance and visual drift source tracking\n\nThe remaining gaps are no longer stage architecture problems. They are mostly automation, enforcement, and minor documentation mirroring work: implementing stricter schema validators, building an automated reference resolver, defining exactly who may accept high or critical risks during agent-run workflows, and mirroring the newest visual-reference compliance terms into older Stage 6-7 review drafts.\n\n---\n\n## Diagnostic Scope\n\nReviewed review docs:\n\n```text\nSystem-References/Docs/Stage-1-product-initialization-draft.md\nSystem-References/Docs/Stage-2-architect.md\nSystem-References/Docs/Stage-3-system-architecture-draft.md\nSystem-References/Docs/Stage-4-ux-interaction-architecture-draft.md\nSystem-References/Docs/Stage-5-development-orchestration-draft.md\nSystem-References/Docs/Stage-6-implementation-validation-draft.md\nSystem-References/Docs/Stage-7-launch-operationalization-draft.md\nSystem-References/Docs/Stage-8-post-launch-evolution-draft.md\nSystem-References/Docs/Global-Stage-Workflow-Contract.md\n```\n\nReviewed Enforces terminal ticket status, validation, repair, visual reference compliance, visual drift source tracking, and artifact evidence. |\n| Stage 7 | `stage-7-launch-operationalization` | `launch-readiness-validation`, `deployment-framework-planning`, `monitoring-systems-planning`, `analytics-framework-planning`, `operational-tooling-planning`, `launch-operationalization-synthesis` | Aligned in live skills. Requires launch readiness, visual reference compliance readiness, and deployment proof controls. |\n| Stage 8 | `stage-8-post-launch-evolution` | `telemetry-analysis`, `operational-optimization`, `ai-improvement-planning`, `roadmap-evolution-planning`, `scalability-evolution-planning`, `post-launch-evolution-synthesis` | Aligned. Routes findings back to owning stages through feedback route candidates. |\n\nFinal synthesis skills are also aligned with their stage gates:\n\n| Stage | Synthesis Skill | Gate Alignment |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Stage 1 | `product-synthesis` | Verifies Stage 1 decision brief before `ready_for_stage_2`. |\n| Stage 2 | `validation-synthesis` | Verifies Stage 2 decision brief and confidence thresholds before `ready_for_stage_3`. |\n| Stage 3 | `architecture-synthesis` | Verifies complete concrete `selected_stack`, rejected alternatives, and approved Stage 3 stack brief before `ready_for_stage_4` or Stage 5 architecture handoff. |\n| Stage 4 | `ux-interaction-synthesis` | Verifies complete app blueprint markdown, selected visual reference continuity, and Stage 4 UX/UI brief before `ready_for_stage_5`. |\n| Stage 5 | `development-orchestration-synthesis` | Acts as final Stage 5 completion gate for `ready_for_stage_6`. |\n| Stage 6 | `system-health-synthesis` | Acts as `post-launch-evolution-synthesis` | Uses `evolution_plan_ready` only after readiness audit passes. |\n\n---\n\n## Workflow Efficiency Assessment\n\n### Planning Phase Efficiency\n\nPlanning phase grade: **98 / 100**\n\nThe planning workflow is now highly efficient because each planning stage has a distinct job and a user confirmation point before the stage is locked:\n\n- Stage 1 defines the app idea, features, MVP, workflows, and assumptions, then asks the user to approve the product direction.\n- Stage 2 validates assumptions using evidence quality and confidence rules, then asks the user to approve whether validation is strong enough to continue.\n- Stage 3 creates architecture from validated assumptions, selects one concrete stack, records rejected alternatives, then asks the user to approve the selected stack.\n- Stage 4 turns UX, screen, UI, complete app blueprint, selected visual references, visual specs, design system, and accessibility requirements into implementation-ready frontend planning, then asks the user to approve the recommended UX/UI direction.\n- Stage 5 converts approved prior outputs into slices, tickets, skill requirements, agents, validation steps, and execution batches.\n\nThe biggest efficiency gain is that Stage 5 no longer has to reinterpret Stage 4 or Stage 3. Tickets can carry upstream references, selected visual style references, required skills, visual requirements, validation requirements, and `expected_artifacts`.\n\n### Implementation Phase Efficiency\n\nImplementation phase grade: **98 / 100**\n\nStage 6 has a strong execution model:\n\n- every ticket must reach a terminal state\n- validation maps back to ticket acceptance criteria\n- failures route into repair loops\n- visual QA is explicit for frontend work\n- visual reference compliance and visual drift source tracking are explicit in the live Stage 6 skills\n- artifacts are recorded or blocked\n- expected artifacts map back to Stage 5 tickets\n- launch-critical work cannot quietly pass with unresolved blockers\n\nThe implementation workflow is ready for multi-agent execution because Stage 5 creates agent context and Stage 6 enforces ticket execution, validation, and repair.\n\n### Launch And Evolution Efficiency\n\nLaunch and evolution grade: **97 / 100**\n\nStage 7 requires real production-readiness proof rather than only launch descriptions. Stage 8 has routing rules that can send live-product findings back to the stage that owns the root cause.\n\nThis creates a complete loop:\n\n```text\nplan -> validate -> architect -> design -> ticket -> build -> launch -> observe -> route feedback\n```\n\n---\n\n## Strongest Workflow Elements\n\n1. **Stage 1-4 proposal-first planning**\n\nThe workflow now asks the user to approve key directions before they become locked stage outputs. This fixes the previous issue where planning could proceed without the user being asked whether they agreed with the direction.\n\n2. **Cognitive stage boundaries**\n\nEach stage owns a distinct reasoning domain and avoids doing downstream work too early.\n\n3. **Global readiness governance**\n\nThe workflow has readiness checks for schemas, artifacts, risk acceptance, reference integrity, revision loops, and now Stage 1-4 decision briefs.\n\n4. **Traceable frontend implementation path**\n\nStage 4 creates UI blueprints, the complete app blueprint tree, selected visual references, visual specs, design system rules, and frontend build packages. Stage 5 turns them into tickets. Stage 6 validates implementation, visual reference compliance, and visual QA. Stage 7 checks visual launch readiness.\n\n5. **Agent-ready development orchestration**\n\nStage 5 can scan skills, assign required skills to tickets, generate agents, create parallel batches, and define validation ownership.\n\n6. **Evidence-backed execution**\n\nArtifact registry and `expected_artifacts` make validation proof durable instead of informal.\n\n7. **Post-launch feedback routing**\n\nStage 8 can route findings to Stage 1-7 instead of treating every live-product problem as a generic roadmap item.\n\n---\n\n## Remaining Gaps\n\n### 1. Automated Schema Validation Is Specified, Not Fully Operationalized\n\nThe docs and commands require `schema_validation`, and schema files exist. The next improvement would be a concrete validator command or skill that checks stage output files against the schemas automatically.\n\nImpact: low to medium.\n\nRecommended future action:\n\n```text\nCreate a schema-validation utility or skill used by global-stage-readiness-audit.\n```\n\n### 2. Reference Integrity Needs An Automated Resolver\n\nThe workflow requires `reference_integrity`, but the actual ID resolution process is still documented rather than implemented as a resolver.\n\nImpact: medium once projects generate large outputs.\n\nRecommended future action:\n\n```text\nCreate a reference-integrity-audit skill that scans stage outputs and verifies ID links.\n```\n\n### 3. Risk Acceptance Ownership Needs A Policy For Agent-Run Workflows\n\nThe risk ledger exists, but future execution should define who can populate `accepted_by` when an autonomous or semi-autonomous agent accepts a risk.\n\nImpact: medium for high-risk projects.\n\nRecommended future action:\n\n```text\nRequire user approval for high and critical accepted risks unless a project policy explicitly delegates that authority.\n```\n\n### 4. Decision Brief Output Generation Could Become A Dedicated Helper\n\nStages 1-4 and their synthesis skills now require decision briefs, but there is no shared helper skill that standardizes formatting and approval capture.\n\nImpact: low.\n\nRecommended future action:\n\n```text\nCreate a stage-decision-brief helper skill only if formatting drift appears across Stage 1-4 outputs.\n```\n\n### 5. Stage 6-7 Review Drafts Need Visual Reference Mirroring\n\nThe live Stage 6 and Stage 7 skills now include visual reference compliance, but the older Stage 6 and Stage 7 review draft documents still mostly describe visual continuity as visual spec plus design system compliance.\n\nImpact: low.\n\nRecommended future action:\n\n```text\nMirror visual_reference_refs, visual_reference_compliance, and visual_drift_source into the Stage 6 and Stage 7 review draft documents.\n```\n\n---\n\n## Current Required Control Coverage\n\n| Control | Stage 1 | Stage 2 | Stage 3 | Stage 4 | Stage 5 | Stage 6 | Stage 7 | Stage 8 |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Stage contract profile | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |\n| Guidance policy | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |\n| Stage decision brief | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A |\n| User approval before lock | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A |\n| Concrete selected stack | N/A | N/A | Yes | Consumes | Consumes | Consumes | Consumes | N/A |\n| Schema reference | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |\n| Schema validation result | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |\n| Reference integrity | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |\n| Risk acceptance ledger | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |\n| Revision loops | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |\n| Artifact registry | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |\n| Readiness audit | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |\n| Visual reference continuity | N/A | N/A | N/A | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Feedback only |\n\n---\n\n## Command Layer Verdict\n\nThe command and synthesis layers are now consistent with the review docs.\n\nKey confirmations:\n\n- Stage 1 command and `product-synthesis` require an app idea/features/MVP decision brief before `ready_for_stage_2`.\n- Stage 2 command and `validation-synthesis` require a validation decision brief before `ready_for_stage_3`.\n- Stage 3 command and `architecture-synthesis` require a complete concrete `selected_stack`, rejected alternatives, and approved stack decision brief before `ready_for_stage_4` or Stage 5 architecture handoff.\n- Stage 4 command and `ux-interaction-synthesis` require selected visual reference continuity, `09-complete-app-blueprint.md`, plus a recommended UX/UI decision brief before `ready_for_stage_5`.\n- Stage 5-8 commands intentionally do not require decision briefs.\n- Stage 5 carries selected visual style references into frontend tickets and agent handoffs through `visual_reference_refs`.\n- Stage 6 live skills validate visual reference compliance and record visual drift source.\n- Stage 7 live skills block launch progression on unresolved visual reference compliance failures unless accepted as launch risk.\n- All stage commands still reference `global-stage-readiness-audit`.\n- Stage 5 still carries `expected_artifacts`.\n- Stage 6 still maps expected artifacts to implementation evidence.\n- Stage 7 still carries deployment proof expectations.\n- Stage 8 still carries feedback routing.\n\n---\n\n## Final Health Verdict\n\nThe Stage 1-8 workflow is now **A-grade and implementation-ready** as an AI app-building harness.\n\nIt can guide a user from:\n\n```text\nraw idea\n-> user-approved product direction\n-> validated assumptions\n-> user-approved concrete architecture stack\n-> user-approved UX/UI, visual reference, and visual blueprint\n-> implementation tickets\n-> agent execution\n-> validation and repair\n-> launch readiness\n-> post-launch evolution\n```\n\nThe next meaningful improvement is not more stage design. The next improvement is automation around the controls already specified:\n\n```text\nschema validation runner\nreference integrity resolver\nrisk acceptance ownership policy\nStage 6-7 visual reference draft mirroring\noptional decision brief helper\n```\n\nCurrent recommended status:\n\n```text\nReady to begin using the Stage 1-8 workflow on a real app plan.\n```\n", (Source: `Rebuilding Stage 4 commands skills.md`)

- [medium] "formatted_output": "# Command — stage-4-ux-interaction-architecture\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `stage-4-ux-interaction-architecture` command orchestrates Stage 4.\n\nIt transforms:\n\n* Stage 1 product workflows\n* Stage 2 validation findings\n* Stage 3 architecture outputs\n* user profiles\n* capabilities and feature structures\n* MVP boundaries\n\ninto:\n\n* user journey architecture\n* interaction architecture\n* screen system architecture\n* feature behavior specifications\n* state transition map\n* accessibility framework\n* implementation-ready UI blueprints\n* frontend build package\n\nThis is the Stage 4 command skill. It is not a single UX subskill.\n\n---\n\n# Cognitive Boundary\n\nStage 4 asks:\n\n```text\nHow should users move through and interact with the validated product?\n```\n\nStage 4 must not:\n\n* redefine the product concept\n* perform market validation\n* redesign backend system architecture\n* write implementation tickets\n* produce final UI art direction as decoration\n* generate frontend code\n* plan engineering sprints\n\nStage 4 may recommend product or architecture revisions only when interaction design exposes a blocking contradiction.\n\n---\n\n# Output Directory\n\nAll final Stage 4 outputs must be recorded in:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-4/\n```\n\nThe command must create this folder if it does not exist.\n\n---\n\n# Shared UX State\n\nThe command maintains a shared Stage 4 UX state object.\n\nThe shared UX state must be written to:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Build-status/UX-state.json\n```\n\nThe command must load this file at the beginning of Stage 4, update it after each UX skill runs, and preserve it as the durable interaction architecture state for the build.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"stage\": \"Stage 4\",\n  \"command\": \"stage-4-ux-interaction-architecture\",\n  \"status\": \"not_started\",\n  \"stage_1_inputs\": {},\n  \"stage_2_inputs\": {},\n  \"stage_3_inputs\": {},\n  \"preflight\": {},\n  \"user_journeys\": \"ux_confidence_gaps\": []\n  },\n  \"stage_5_handoff\": {},\n  \"completion_status\": {}\n}\n```\n\nEach subskill reads the current UX state and writes its updates back into the shared state before the next skill runs.\n\nAfter each subskill completes, the command must persist the updated shared state to:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Build-status/UX-state.json\n```\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Rules\n\nThe Stage 4 command should behave like a guided interaction design interview.\n\nUse this decision rule:\n\n```text\nAsk only for UX decisions that materially affect user journeys, interaction behavior, screen structure, accessibility, or Stage 5 implementation planning.\nInfer standard interaction defaults when risk is low and the product workflow supports the inference.\nRecord assumptions when proceeding without user confirmation.\nBlock only when a missing decision prevents coherent interaction architecture.\n```\n\nWhen asking the user questions:\n\n* ask 1-3 questions at a time\n* prioritize workflow-blocking or accessibility-critical questions first\n* avoid asking questions already answered by Stage 1, Stage 2, or Stage 3 outputs\n* explain what journey, screen, state, or behavior each question affects\n* prefer concrete options over open-ended questions when the tradeoff is known\n* update `interactive_guidance.open_questions`\n* move answered questions into `interactive_guidance.answered_questions`\n* record inferred defaults in `interactive_guidance.assumptions_made`\n* record unresolved blockers in `interactive_guidance.blocked_decisions`\n\nThe command should continue automatically when a UX decision has a low-risk default.\n\nThe command should pause for user input when:\n\n* primary user journey is unclear\n* user role differences change screens or permissions\n* a workflow has no clear start, success, or failure state\n* feature behavior depends on an unresolved product decision\n* accessibility requirements materially affect interaction design\n* the screen system cannot support a core workflow\n* a Stage 3 architecture constraint changes user interaction\n\nThe command should not ask the user to choose implementation details that belong to Stage 5 unless the decision changes Stage 4 interaction architecture.\n\nFor every created page, infer a complete interactive element proposal before asking the user. A created page is any page or screen recorded in `page_inventory` or `ui_blueprints`.\n\nClassify each created page as:\n\n```text\nlaunch_critical\nstandard\nsupporting\ndeferred\n```\n\nPresent the proposed interactive elements for approval only when the choice materially changes workflow scope, permissions, destructive behavior, route or action outcomes, accessibility, or Stage 5 implementation. Ask the user to approve, remove, rename, reroute, or add elements. Record low-risk inferred elements in `interactive_guidance.assumptions_made`.\n\nEvery page interaction contract must use one approval status:\n\n```text\napproved\nassumed_low_risk\nneeds_user_review\nblocked\n```\n\n---\n\n# Stage 4 Input Contract\n\nLoad Stage 1 outputs from:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-1/\n```\n\nLoad Stage 2 outputs from:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-2/\n```\n\nLoad Stage 3 outputs from:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-3/\n```\n\nRequired Stage 1 files:\n\n```text\n02-user-system-map.json\n03-workflow-architecture.json\n04-product-capabilities.json\n05-feature-structure.json\n06-product-boundaries.json\n08-mvp-operational-model.json\n10-success-framework.json\n```\n\nRequired Stage 2 files:\n\n```text\n01-market-analysis.json\n05-risk-validation.json\n06-strategic-positioning.json\n```\n\nRequired Stage 3 files:\n\n```text\n01-system-topology.json\n02-service-architecture.json\n03-data-architecture.json\n04-api-architecture.json\n06-security-foundations.json\n08-scalability-framework.json\n```\n\nMinimum viable input set:\n\n```text\nStage 1:\n02-user-system-map.json\n03-workflow-architecture.json\n05-feature-structure.json\n08-mvp-operational-model.json\n\nStage 3:\n01-system-topology.json\n03-data-architecture.json\n04-api-architecture.json\n", (Source: `Rebuilding Stage 4 commands skills.md`)

cognition\n```\n\nNOT:\n\n* product discovery\n* market validation\n* system architecture\n* implementation scheduling\n* visual polish as decoration\n\nThose responsibilities belong to other stages.\n\nStage 4 is responsible for transforming validated product and technical architecture into a coherent human interaction model.\n\nThe stage focuses on:\n\n* user journeys\n* interaction architecture\n* screen systems\n* feature behavior\n* state transitions\n* accessibility foundations\n* interface consistency\n\n---\n\n# Stage 4 Core Purpose\n\nTransform:\n\n* Stage 1 product workflows\n* Stage 2 validation findings\n* Stage 3 architecture outputs\n* user profiles\n* capabilities and feature structures\n* MVP boundaries\n\ninto:\n\n* user journey architecture\n* interaction architecture\n* screen system architecture\n* feature behavior specifications\n* state transition map\n* accessibility framework\n\n---\n\n# Recommended Stage 4 Architecture\n\n```text\nstage-4-ux-interaction-architecture (command)\n│\n├── user-journey-design\n├── interaction-architecture-design\n├── screen-system-design\n├── feature-behavior-specification\n├── state-transition-and-accessibility-design\n├── ui-blueprint-specification\n├── design-system-foundation\n└── ux-interaction-synthesis\n```\n\n---\n\n# Stage 4 Command\n\n# Command — stage-4-ux-interaction-architecture\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `stage-4-ux-interaction-architecture` command orchestrates Stage 4.\n\nIt transforms product, validation, and system architecture intelligence into a UX and interaction architecture package that is ready for Stage 5 development orchestration.\n\nStage 4 must also transform UX requirements into implementation-ready UI blueprints that can be consumed by frontend design skills, frontend builder skills, task generators, and agent builders without generating frontend code.\n\nThis is the Stage 4 command skill. It is not a single UX subskill.\n\n---\n\n# Cognitive Boundary\n\nStage 4 asks:\n\n```text\nHow should users move through and interact with the validated product?\n```\n\nStage 4 must not:\n\n* redefine the product concept\n* perform market validation\n* redesign backend system architecture\n* write implementation tickets\n* produce final UI art direction as decoration\n* generate frontend code\n* plan engineering sprints\n\nStage 4 may recommend product or architecture revisions only when interaction design exposes a blocking contradiction.\n\n---\n\n# Output Directory\n\nAll final Stage 4 outputs must be recorded in:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-4/\n```\n\nThe command must create this folder if it does not exist.\n\n---\n\n# Shared UX State\n\nThe command maintains a shared Stage 4 UX state object.\n\nThe shared UX state must be written to:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Build-status/UX-state.json\n```\n\nThe command must load this file at the beginning of Stage 4, update it after each UX skill runs, and preserve it as the durable interaction architecture state for the build.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"stage\": \"Stage 4\",\n  \"command\": \"interaction_tradeoffs\": [],\n  \"open_questions\": [],\n  \"interactive_guidance\": {\n    \"open_questions\": [],\n    \"answered_questions\": [],\n    \"assumptions_made\": [],\n    \"blocked_decisions\": [],\n    \"user_confirmations\": [],\n    \"ux_confidence_gaps\": []\n  },\n  \"stage_5_handoff\": {},\n  \"completion_status\": {}\n}\n```\n\nEach subskill reads the current UX state and writes its updates back into the shared state before the next skill runs.\n\nAfter each subskill completes, the command must persist the updated shared state to:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Build-status/UX-state.json\n```\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Rules\n\nThe Stage 4 command should behave like a guided interaction design interview.\n\nUse this decision rule:\n\n```text\nAsk only for UX decisions that materially affect user journeys, interaction behavior, screen structure, accessibility, or Stage 5 implementation planning.\nInfer standard interaction defaults when risk is low and the product workflow supports the inference.\nRecord assumptions when proceeding without user confirmation.\nBlock only when a missing decision prevents coherent interaction architecture.\n```\n\nWhen asking the user questions:\n\n* ask 1-3 questions at a time\n* prioritize workflow-blocking or accessibility-critical questions first\n* avoid asking questions tradeoff is known\n* update `interactive_guidance.open_questions`\n* move answered questions into `interactive_guidance.answered_questions`\n* record inferred defaults in `interactive_guidance.assumptions_made`\n* record unresolved blockers in `interactive_guidance.blocked_decisions`\n\nThe command should continue automatically when a UX decision has a low-risk default.\n\nThe command should pause for user input when:\n\n* primary user journey is unclear\n* user role differences change screens or permissions\n* a workflow has no clear start, success, or architecture.\n\n---\n\n# Stage 4 Input Contract\n\nLoad Stage 1 outputs from:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-1/\n```\n\nLoad Stage 2 outputs from:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-2/\n```\n\nLoad Stage 3 outputs from:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-3/\n```\n\nRequired Stage 1 files:\n\n```text\n02-user-system-map.json\n03-workflow-architecture.json\n04-product-capabilities.json\n05-feature-structure.json\n06-product-boundaries.json\n08-mvp-operational-model.json\n10-success-framework.json\n```\n\nRequired has an inclusion rationale tied to upstream product, workflow, role, feature, journey, or route evidence\n* every launch-critical page has a visual spec\n* every launch-critical visual spec includes visual acceptance criteria and user approval status\n* design system foundation exists for launch-critical frontend work\n* visual reference selections are traceable into design system rules, UI blueprint visual specs, and Stage 5 handoff\n* every created page enumerates every interactive element per component per section\n* every element has a stable ID, owner, label or accessible name, behavior, source trace, and route, action, or `no_navigation` classification\n* every internal navigation target resolves to route_inventory and every external target is explicitly classified\n* action_inventory covers all created pages and records triggering elements and outcomes\n* route_inventory covers all navigation and action targets\n* navigation items have structured route_target entries that resolve\n* destructive and permission-gated interactions have confirmation, denied, and recovery behavior where applicable\n* clickable containers do not conflict with nested buttons or row actions\n* duplicate labels do not map to conflicting behavior without contextual accessible names\n* required Mermaid maps reconcile with page, element, route, and action IDs\n* UI blueprints are usable by Stage 5 development orchestration\n* complete app blueprint markdown is usable by Stage 5 without reinterpreting page, component, route, action, state, or data requirements\n* every core workflow has states and recovery behavior\n* accessibility risks are recorded\n* critical interactive guidance questions are answered or converted into recorded assumptions\n* Stage 5 handoff is usable for development orchestration\n* Stage 4 decision brief approval is recorded before Stage 5 handoff is used\n\nBefore using `ready_for_stage_5`, this skill must generate or verify:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-4/00-stage-decision-brief.md\n```\n\nIf the decision brief is not approved, return the recommended UX/UI direction for user review instead of locking Stage 4.\n\nBefore using `ready_for_stage_5`, this skill must also generate or verify:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-4/09-complete-app-blueprint.md\n```\n\nIf the complete app blueprint is missing, incomplete, or does not map launch-critical pages to `ui_blueprint_id` values, return the blueprint gaps for revision before locking Stage 4.\n", (Source: `Rebuilding Stage 4 commands skills.md`)

- [medium] "formatted_output": "# UI-COMPONENT.md System Build Plan\n\n## 1. System Goal\n\nBuild a reusable system that generates a project-specific `UI-COMPONENTS.md` file from a selected UI architecture template.\n\nThe system should help define:\n\n* Application navigation\n* Application shell\n* Page hierarchy\n* Page layouts\n* Grid, table, list, and card usage\n* Component families\n* Interaction patterns\n* Responsive behavior\n* Loading, empty, error, and permission states\n* Accessibility expectations\n\nThe system should work independently from visual design styles.\n\nExample:\n\n```yaml\nui_architecture_template: saas-dashboard\nvisual_design_template: neobrutalism\n```\n\nThe UI architecture template determines structure and behavior.\n\nThe design template determines colors, typography, borders, shadows, and visual styling.\n\n---\n\n# 2. Final System Shape\n\nThe completed system should contain five major parts:\n\n```text\nUI-COMPONENT.md System\n├── Template schema\n├── UI architecture templates\n├── Template selector\n├── Project file generator\n└── Validation system\n```\n\nRecommended directory structure:\n\n```text\nui-component-system/\n├── README.md\n├── TEMPLATE-SCHEMA.md\n├── TEMPLATE-SELECTOR.md\n├── GENERATION-WORKFLOW.md\n├── OUTPUT-SCHEMA.md\n├── NORMALIZED-VALUES.md\n│\n├── templates/\n│   ├── base/\n│   │   └── base-ui-architecture.md\n│   ├── websites/\n│   ├── web-apps/\n│   ├── commerce/\n│   └── mobile/\n│\n├── patterns/\n│   ├── navigation/\n│   ├── layouts/\n│   ├── pages/\n│   ├── components/\n│   ├── interactions/\n│   └── states/\n│\n├── extensions/\n│   ├── analytics.md\n│   ├── collaboration.md\n│   ├── role-based-access.md\n│   └── onboarding.md\n│\n├── assets/\n│   └── UI-COMPONENTS.template.md\n│\n├── validation/\n│   ├── TEMPLATE-CHECKLIST.md\n│   ├── OUTPUT-CHECKLIST.md\n│   └── CONTRADICTION-RULES.md\n│\n└── tests/\n    ├── test-projects/\n    ├── expected-outputs/\n    └── TEST-RESULTS.md\n```\n\n---\n\n# Phase 1 — Define the System Boundaries\n\n## Step 1. Define what `UI-COMPONENTS.md` controls\n\nCreate a document that explicitly defines the file’s responsibilities.\n\nThe file should control:\n\n```yaml\nui_components_responsibilities:\n  - information-architecture\n  - application-navigation\n  - application-shell\n  - page-inventory\n  - page-archetypes\n  - page-layouts\n  - component-selection\n  - responsive-behavior\n  - interaction-patterns\n  - system-states\n  - accessibility-structure\n```\n\nThe file should not control:\n\n```yaml\nexcluded_responsibilities:\n  - final-color-palette\n  - typography-branding\n  - logo-treatment\n  - illustration-style\n  - backend-architecture\n  - database-schema\n  - API-design\n  - feature-requirements\n```\n\n## Step 2. Define the relationship with other project files\n\nCreate a clear document ownership map.\n\n```yaml\nproject_files:\n  PRD.md:\n    defines: product-requirements\n\n  USER-FLOWS.md:\n    defines: user-task-sequences\n\n  UI-COMPONENTS.md:\n    defines: interface-structure-and-behavior\n\n  DESIGN.md:\n    defines: visual-design-language\n\n  TECH-STACK.md:\n    defines: implementation-technology\n```\n\n## Step 3. Define the system terminology\n\nStandardize terms early.\n\nUse:\n\n```yaml\nterminology:\n  ui_template: A reusable structural architecture\n  page_archetype: A reusable page type\n  layout_pattern: A method of arranging page content\n  component_family: A group of related reusable components\n  extension: An optional capability added to a base template\n  project_output: The generated UI-COMPONENTS.md file\n  override: A project-specific replacement for a template default\n```\n\n## Phase 1 deliverables\n\n```text\nREADME.md\nDOCUMENT-BOUNDARIES.md\nTERMINOLOGY.md\n```\n\n---\n\n# Phase 2 — Build the Universal Template Schema\n\n## Step 4. Create `TEMPLATE-SCHEMA.md`\n\nEvery UI architecture template must use the same structure.\n\nRequired template sections:\n\n```text\n1. Template identity\n2. Product characteristics\n3. Structural defaults\n4. Information architecture\n5. Navigation architecture\n6. Application shell\n7. Page archetypes\n8. Page composition patterns\n9. Layout rules\n10. Component families\n11. Interaction patterns\n12. Responsive strategy\n13. System states\n14. Accessibility requirements\n15. Adaptation rules\n16. Output instructions\n```\n\n## Step 5. Define template metadata\n\nUse a standard frontmatter block.\n\n```yaml\n---\ntemplate_id: saas-dashboard\ntemplate_name: SaaS Dashboard\ncategory: web-app\nversion: 1.0.0\nstatus: stable\n", (Source: `Rebuilding Stage 4 commands skills.md`)

- [medium] "formatted_output": "# Skill — ui-blueprint-specification\n\n# Purpose\n\nThe `ui-blueprint-specification` skill transforms Stage 4 UX requirements into implementation-ready UI blueprints without generating frontend code.\n\nIt defines:\n\n* pages\n* screens\n* layouts\n* components\n* navigation\n* user actions\n* forms\n* tables\n* cards\n* modals\n* drawers\n* loading states\n* empty states\n* error states\n* frontend build package inputs\n\nThis skill is the bridge between Stage 4 UX architecture and Stage 5 frontend implementation planning.\n\nIt consumes the selected Stage 4 design system and visual references from `design-system-foundation`. It applies those decisions per page instead of inventing a separate visual direction for each blueprint.\n\n---\n\n# Operating Rule\n\nDo not ask broad questions such as:\n\n```text\nWhat should this dashboard look like?\n```\n\nForce every launch-critical page through the page-definition matrix:\n\n```text\nPAGE\nPurpose\nPrimary User\nScreen Type\nLayout Type\nSections\nComponents\nActions\nData Needed\nStates\nValidation\nNavigation\n```\n\nThen force every launch-critical page through the visual spec matrix:\n\n```text\nVISUAL SPEC\nVisual Style\nDesign System Refs\nVisual Reference Refs\nDensity\nColor Direction\nTypography Feel\nComponent Style\nPrimary Visual Focus\nResponsive Behavior\nVisual Do Rules\nVisual Don't Rules\nReference Apps\nDesign System Alignment\nVisual Acceptance Criteria\nUser Approval Status\n```\n\n---\n\n# Controlled Choices\n\nScreen type options:\n\n```text\nDashboard\nList\nDetail View\nForm\nWizard\nSettings\nProfile\nAnalytics\nMessaging\nLanding Page\nHero Page\nMarketing Page\nOnboarding\nPricing\nAuthentication\nAdmin\nCheckout\nCustom\n```\n\nScreen/page type selection must be contextual.\n\nThese options are a controlled vocabulary, not a required checklist. Include only page or screen types justified by:\n\n* Stage 1 product category and MVP scope\n* Stage 1 workflows and feature structure\n* Stage 3 selected stack and architecture constraints\n* Stage 4 user journeys and launch-critical interactions\n* user roles, permissions, and navigation needs\n\nDo not add `Landing Page`, `Hero Page`, `Dashboard`, `Admin`, `Checkout`, `Authentication`, `Pricing`, or any other page type unless the product model requires it.\n\nFor each selected page type, record:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"page_name\": \"\",\n  \"screen_type\": \"\",\n  \"included_because\": [],\n  \"source_refs\": [],\n  \"excluded_page_types\": [\n    {\n      \"screen_type\": \"\",\n      \"reason\": \"\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nAsk the user only when a launch-critical page type is ambiguous. Otherwise infer the page type from upstream workflow, role, feature, and route evidence, and record the assumption.\n\nLayout type options:\n\n```text\nSidebar\nTop Navigation\nSplit View\nCard Grid\nTable\nMobile First\nFull Screen\nCustom\n```\n\nComponent options:\n\n```text\nCards\nCharts\nTables\nSearch\nFilters\nForms\nTabs\nModals\nDrawers\nNotifications\nFile Upload\nComments\nTimeline\nMaps\nCalendar\n```\n\nAction options:\n\n```text\nCreate\nRead\nUpdate\nDelete\nExport\nShare\nInvite\nApprove\nReject\nUpload\nDownload\n```\n\nVisual style options:\n\n```text\nMinimal\nEnterprise\nEditorial\nConsumer App\nSaaS Dashboard\nData Dense\nPlayful\nLuxury\nUtility\nCustom\n```\n\nDensity options:\n\n```text\nCompact\nBalanced\nSpacious\nData Dense\nMobile First\nCustom\n```\n\nComponent style options:\n\n```text\nFlat\nOutlined\nSoft Card\nHigh Contrast\nDense Utility\nMedia Rich\nCustom\n```\n\n---\n\n# Complete App Blueprint Markdown\n\nGenerate a readable complete app blueprint tree at:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-4/09-complete-app-blueprint.md\n```\n\nThe markdown tree must use this structure, adapted to the app being built. The example page names below are illustrative only; the generated tree must include the pages required by the actual product:\n\n```text\nComplete App Blueprint\n│\n├── Pages\n│   ├── Example Landing Page\n│   │   ├── Hero\n│   │   ├── Feature Preview\n│   │   ├── CTA\n│   │   └── Footer\n│   ├── Example Dashboard\n│   │   ├── Summary Cards\n│   │   ├── Activity Feed\n│   │   └── Task Table\n│\n├── Components\n│\n├── Shared Components\n│\n├── Navigation\n│\n├── Routes\n│\n├── Actions\n│\n├── States\n│\n├── Data Requirements\n│\n└── Frontend Build Package\n```\n\nEvery launch-critical page in the markdown tree must map to a `ui_blueprint_id` and include its sections, components, primary actions, route, states, and data requirements.\n\nThe complete app blueprint must also include:\n\n* one compact Mermaid app route map covering every created page\n* page-level Mermaid interaction maps for launch-critical or complex pages\n* critical workflow Mermaid maps that include success, failure, and recovery branches\n* destructive or mutation Mermaid maps that include confirmation and result states\n\nRequire a page-level Mermaid map when a page has multiple interaction branches, destructive or mutation actions, modal or drawer flows, or complex routing. A trivial page may rely on its interaction contract and inventories when the app route map already covers it.\n\n---\n\n# Visual Hierarchy Model\n\nEach page blueprint must preserve:\n\n```text\nPage\n├─ Section\n│  ├─ Component\n│  │  ├─ Interactive Element\n│  │  │  └─ Route, Action, Or No Navigation\n│  │  ├─ Data Source\n│  │  ├─ Validation\n│  │  └─ States\n```\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Element Schema\n\nEvery interactive element on a page (button, link, icon button, menu item, tab, input, etc.) must be enumerated with:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"element_id\": \"UI-ELEMENT-001\",\n  \"element_type\": \"button | link | icon_button | menu_item | tab | toggle | checkbox | radio | select | text_input | search_input | file_upload | date_picker | breadcrumb | pagination | clickable_card | clickable_row | disclosure\",\n  \"label\": \"\",\n  \"accessible_name\": \"\",\n  \"icon\": \"\",\n  \"owning_page_ref\": \"\",\n  \"owning_section_ref\": \"\",\n  \"owning_component_ref\": \"\",\n  \"route_id\": \"\",\n  \"route_target\": \"\",\n  \"route_type\": \"internal_page | external_url | modal | drawer | anchored_section | file_download | api_action | state_transition | no_navigation\",\n  \"action_id\": \"ACTION-001\",\n  \"behavior\": \"navigate | submit | open_modal | open_drawer | toggle | trigger_action | open_link | download | call_api | scroll_to | no_navigation\",\n  \"behavior_target\": \"\",\n  \"design_system_component\": \"\",\n  \"states\": {\n    \"default\": {},\n    \"loading\": {},\n    \"disabled\": {},\n    \"active\": {},\n    \"hover\": {}\n  },\n  \"permission_required\": \"\",\n  \"permission_denied_behavior\": \"\",\n  \"confirmation_required\": false,\n  \"responsive_behavior\": {},\n  \"accessibility_behavior\": {},\n  \"analytics_event\": \"\",\n  \"source_trace\": []\n}\n```\n\n# Action Inventory Schema\n\nEvery action across all pages must be recorded in a global action inventory:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"action_id\": \"ACTION-001\",\n  \"name\": \"\",\n  \"element_type\": \"button | link | icon_button | menu_item | tab | toggle | checkbox | radio | select\",\n  \"label\": \"\",\n  \"route_target\": \"\",\n  \"behavior\": \"navigate | submit | open_modal | open_drawer | toggle | trigger_action | open_link | download | call_api | scroll_to\",\n  \"behavior_target\": \"\",\n  \"owning_page_refs\": [],\n  \"owning_component_refs\": [],\n  \"triggering_element_refs\": [],\n  \"permission_required\": \"\",\n  \"confirmation_required\": false,\n  \"success_destination\": \"\",\n  \"failure_destination\": \"\",\n  \"loading_state\": \"\",\n  \"empty_state\": \"\",\n  \"permission_denied_behavior\": \"\",\n  \"undo_or_recovery_path\": \"\",\n  \"states\": {},\n  \"analytics_event\": \"\",\n  \"source_trace\": []\n}\n```\n\n# Route Inventory Schema\n\nEvery route across all pages must be recorded in a global route inventory:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"route_id\": \"ROUTE-001\",\n  \"path\": \"\",\n  \"page_ref\": \"\",\n  \"page_name\": \"\",\n  \"screen_type\": \"\",\n  \"is_launch_critical\": false,\n  \"role_access\": [],\n  \"owning_journey_ids\": [],\n  \"related_routes\": [],\n  \"source_trace\": []\n}\n```\n\n# Navigation Inventory Schema\n\nEvery navigation item across the app must be recorded:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"nav_item_id\": \"\",\n  \"label\": \"\",\n  \"route_target\": \"\",\n  \"icon\": \"\",\n  \"order\": 0,\n  \"group\": \"\",\n  \"permission_required\": \"\",\n  \"children\": [],\n  \"owning_page_refs\": []\n}\n```\n\n# Page Interaction Contract\n\nCreate one compact contract for every page recorded in `page_inventory` or `ui_blueprints`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"page_ref\": \"\",\n  \"ui_blueprint_id\": \"UI-BLUEPRINT-001\",\n  \"route_id\": \"ROUTE-001\",\n  \"criticality\": \"launch_critical | standard | supporting | deferred\",\n  \"interactive_element_count\": 0,\n  \"interactive_element_refs\": [],\n  \"unresolved_element_refs\": [],\n  \"assumptions\": [],\n  \"approval_status\": \"approved | assumed_low_risk | needs_user_review | blocked\",\n  \"mermaid_map_required\": false\n}\n```\n\nApply deeper design-system, mobile, accessibility, state, and user-confirmation detail to launch-critical pages. Apply confirmation, success, failure, loading, permission-denied, undo, and recovery detail to destructive, security-sensitive, payment, admin, permission-sensitive, and mutation actions.\n\n---\n\n# Interactive Guidance Responsibilities\n\nAsk the user to confirm or choose:\n\n* screen type\n* layout type\n* sections\n* components\n* user actions\n* required states\n* shared components\n* route and navigation expectations\n* visual style\n* density\n* color direction\n* typography feel\n* component style\n* primary visual focus\n* visual do and don't rules\n* visual acceptance criteria\n* user approval status\n\nInfer the full interactive element inventory before asking. Present the proposal and ask the user to approve, remove, rename, reroute, or add elements only when the decision is material. Do not ask the broad question \"what interactive elements should be on this page?\".\n\nAsk no more than 1-3 page-definition questions at once.\n\nInfer common UI patterns when strongly implied by screen type and workflow, but record assumptions in:\n\n```text\ninteractive_guidance.assumptions_made\n```\n\nPause for user input when:\n\n* a launch-critical page lacks purpose\n* a screen type cannot be inferred\n* layout choice materially affects navigation or implementation\n* required components or actions are ambiguous\n* required states are missing for a launch-critical interaction\n* visual style, density, or primary visual focus is missing for a launch-critical page\n* the user has not approved the visual spec for a launch-critical page\n\n---\n\n# Inputs\n\n```json\n{\n  \"user_journeys\": {},\n  \"interaction_architecture\": {},\n  \"screen_system\": {},\n  \"feature_behaviors\": {},\n  \"state_transition_map\": {},\n  \"accessibility_framework\": {},\n  \"design_system_foundation\": {},\n  \"visual_reference_selection\": {},\n  \"existing_state\": {}\n}\n```\n\nRead and update shared UX state from:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Build-status/UX-state.json\n```\n\n---\n\n# Outputs\n\nWrite or update:\n\n```text\nBuild-Plans/Stage-4/07-ui-blueprint-specification.json\n```\n\nThe output must include:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"stage\": \"Stage 4\",\n  \"status\": \"\",\n  \"ui_blueprints\": [],\n  \"page_inventory\": [],\n  \"interaction_contracts\": [],\n  \"interactive_element_inventory\":
